name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: The 51st vote
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240731%2E444211%2Eq8Nlj-)
It’s some powerful poetic justice that Texas — for decades written off by national Democrats and taken for granted by national Republicans — might tip the balance of power in this country at its most critical moment of truth.
James Talarico won a commanding victory last night, generating outsized enthusiasm across the state. From the Rio Grande Valley to the Panhandle, El Paso to Austin, he not only won county after county, but he helped generate turnout numbers that we haven’t seen in decades.
And it wasn’t easy. Jasmine Crockett is one of the most exciting Democrats Texas has produced, a real fighter who made a name for herself standing up to Trump and representing a fierce independence that also helped drive record turnout throughout the state.
What about Republicans? Though John Cornyn edged ahead of Ken Paxton in last night’s Republican primary, they are now both headed for a costly runoff. They’ve already spent more than $90 million tearing each other apart, and it will only get more expensive and nastier heading into the May 26th runoff election.
After conceding to Talarico today, Crockett has asked her supporters to rally behind him and all Democrats on the ballot. That means we have the two strongest Democrats in the state on the same team, working together at time that Republicans are fighting, fractured and months away from a nominee.
In addition, Democrats now have a nominee for every Congressional seat, every State House seat and every State Senate seat for the first time since 1974. That means that behind James are nearly 200 strong, local candidates who are pulling in new voters from across the 254 counties of Texas.
These dynamics play out as Trump grows more unpopular. His policies of kicking people off Medicaid, hurting farmers and ranchers through tariffs, raiding communities and separating families with ICE agents and putting military families in harm’s way through another war of choice in the Middle East will all stick to Republican nominees, including whoever emerges from the Senate primary runoff.
Though we are still awaiting full election-day data, the results from early voting show record-shattering turnout across the state, eclipsing peak presidential election year numbers. And most gratifying, young voter turnout is way up. These are the voters I spend my time with, volunteering alongside other Powered by People volunteers to reach, register and stay in touch with 18-29 year olds to dramatically increase the likelihood that they’ll vote.
That means that the special election results in Tarrant County in January — where a Democrat won a Trump +17 district — were not an anomaly but instead a harbinger of what was revealed last night, and what we can expect to see in November if we put in the work and keep up the fight.
These results are not lost on Trump. He understands that if he loses Texas, he loses his presidency. His cronies and corrupt friends lose the effective immunity with which they’ve operated this criminal operation out of the White House. They lose protection from subpoena, they lose the ability to defy the Constitution, defraud the American people. They lose the ability to destroy this democracy and deliver Trump or his chosen successor a third term in 2028.
He will do everything in his power to steal November’s election in Texas before the first votes are cast. He will attempt to cancel mail-in voting, purge voters from the rolls, “nationalize” our elections.
We must be ready for the fight — doing everything we can, with what we have, where we are.
That means registering young voters and staying in touch with them, to help them navigate the voter suppression that already exists in Texas and anticipating new forms of suppression that are sure to come. Powered by People — the organization I lead — is doing this work every single day in Texas.
Today we’ll be helping students at Texas A&M get registered and ready to vote in November, tomorrow we’ll be at University of Houston. Join us as a volunteer, there are options for those who want to do the work in person or remotely from home or another state: [poweredxpeople.org](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=3&akid=240731%2E444211%2Eq8Nlj-)
It also means getting behind James Talarico and our other Democratic nominees with all we’ve got. [You can donate to James’ campaign here.](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/67608?refcode=ema20260304-240731&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=240731%2E444211%2Eq8Nlj-)
If we meet this moment with what it takes, if Democrats show this same fight across the country — winning Senate races in Georgia, Michigan, North Carolina and Maine — James Talarico will be the 51st vote in the U.S. Senate.
Let’s make it happen.
Thank you,
Beto

Peter, I was on MS NOW after winning North Carolina’s Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate.
Like I said on air, I want to be a Senator for that working parent who’s spending more than she can afford on groceries. I want to be a Senator for those who are finding health care too expensive. I’m running because I can’t stay on the sidelines when I see what is happening in our country. I hope you won’t either.
I’m fighting with everything I have to flip this seat from red to blue for the first time since 2008 and help Democrats take back the Senate. **[_But this is set to be the most competitive and expensive race of 2026, so my team and I have set a goal to raise $1 million to kick off our general election campaign. Please, chip in what you can right now to help us win in North Carolina._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6725?t=8&akid=694%2E124072%2EncJPuq)**
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6725?t=9&akid=694%2E124072%2EncJPuq)

Far-right Republicans like my opponent, Michael Whatley, are attempting to rip away our fundamental rights. The right to vote. To live free of discrimination. To access an abortion. To get a quality education.
I’m in this race to fight for our values, our rights and our families’ futures. To deliver health care access, good job opportunities, strong public schools and so much more to communities across the country – because that’s what Americans deserve.
**[_Together, I know we can defeat my MAGA opponent and fix what’s broken in Washington DC. So please, will you invest $5 or more today to help us reach our $1 million general election goal and set our campaign up for success?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6725?t=10&akid=694%2E124072%2EncJPuq)**

– Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

The implications for the upcoming midterms are huge. None of that includes bills filed in legislatures that already started sessions in January, either. It's all part of a pattern two decades in the making. Now that we’re through the primary, far-right Republicans will pour millions more into our race to try and prevent that from happening. While I’ve never lost an election, I need the support of people like you to win again. We cannot run the risk of Trump’s handpicked candidate getting to the U.S. Senate and helping the GOP hold on to power any longer.** I’m grateful to have you on this team. Thank you. Roy Cooper If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support.

Peter, Since Trump and his MAGA allies catapulted the country into a redistricting crisis last year, we’ve been warning about the chaos and voter suppression that would likely follow. **What happened last night in Texas is exactly what we were worried about. **
* Since redistricting in December, the state’s official website has not been updated and included inaccurate voting locations.
* In Dallas County, there was so much confusion over voting rules that the county’s election site crashed.
* Hundreds of voters in two counties were turned away at polling locations and told to go to different precincts.
* Because of that widespread confusion, a judge ordered the polls to stay open until 9 p.m.
* However, the Texas Supreme Court then put a hold on that ruling and called for ballots cast after 7 p.m. to be “separated” — ultimately, those votes may not be counted at all.

Attorney General Eric Holder had this to say about last night’s Texas nightmare: “Texas is close to not being a functioning democracy. It’s the hardest place to vote because Republicans have put impediments in place based on totally bogus vote fraud concerns — that they just make up. The courts have become complicit in this effort. What we’re seeing in Texas now is a disgrace.” [**This is why we must fight tooth and nail to stop efforts to interfere with voting rights — because they have no place in representative democracy. Because of that widespread confusion, a judge ordered the polls to stay open until 9 p.m. However, the Texas Supreme Court then put a hold on that ruling and called for ballots cast after 7 p.m. to be “separated” — ultimately, those votes may not be counted at all. Attorney General Eric Holder had this to say about last night’s Texas nightmare: “Texas is close to not being a functioning democracy. It’s the hardest place to vote because Republicans have put impediments in place based on totally bogus vote fraud concerns — that they just make up. The courts have become complicit in this effort. # [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40935%2E3422442%2EIpp2ec)
Peter,
Who we elect as California’s next Governor is the biggest, most powerful statement we can make in 2026 about who we are as Democrats.
Let’s elect a bold leader who will do the big things we have long fought for. When I’m Governor, I will deliver:
**Single-payer health care** because I’ve fought for Medicare for All my entire career, and I won’t give up as California’s next governor.
**Less expensive housing** so everyone can afford to start a family, career, or retire in California.
**Free child care for all** so our economy can grow and parents don’t have to choose between their jobs or their kids.
**Zero tuition charges at the University of California and California State University** so Californians can get a world-class education without being crushed by student loan debt.
**No California income taxes for those earning less than $100,000** to put thousands of dollars back in families' pockets.
Those are _real affordability solutions._
I am running for Governor because I am willing and ready to get those things done, unlike **my corporate-backed opponents who are running to help special interests, not working families.**
**[Peter, I need you with me if we’re going to pass these bold, progressive policies. Can you chip in $5 to my campaign today to help us out?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260304_1_ak.1yMxr7&refcode=em20260304-40935&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=40935%2E3422442%2EIpp2ec)**

body:
Help Dan Cox remove Wes Moore from the governor's office with your donation today and stop his land and grocery grab. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/coxforcongress/dan-cox-files-public-information-act-requests-seeking-governor-moores-communications-with-maryland-electric-utilities-and-pjm-interconnection-6753078?e=5bb5efcda7)

| |
---
| |
# Wes Moore's Land and Grocery Grab
HELP DAN CAMPAIGN FOR GOVERNOR TO STAND UP FOR MARYLANDERS
[](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=ea837118c2&e=5bb5efcda7) Annapolis, Maryland — Wes Moore has submitted legislation to seize authority away from local and county officials in zoning matters in order to override them and authorize packed in up-zoned dense housing in and near established and quiet communities. And his bill to establish price fixing for groceries will potentially limit coupons and sales and make such illegal.

**Dear friend of Maryland,**

The Moore initiatives are a knee-jerk and likely unconstitutional response to Maryland's housing and cost of living crisis, which Wes Moore is making worse by raising tax assessment values last year by over 20%.

And his bill on "protection from predatory pricing" has been shown by local grocery stores to risk preventing consumers from receiving coupon and discount deals as it is focused on price fixing, rather than lowering costs to the the grocer.

That means that renters and property owners alike are now paying about $100-$200 minimum a month more in property taxes or rent costs. Landowners pass along to tenants the costs of service billed by the authorities. And food and grocery costs are likely to continue to be extremely high, fixed by government.

I have a different plan that will immediately lower housing costs and cost of living including groceries.

My administration will work to eliminate property taxes beginning with freezing valuation taxation at the price you paid to buy the home, helping renters as well with the stability of no annual increases because of taxation on so-called unrealized gains.

And by freezing taxes and fees in the State, and slashing electric bills through getting rid of the green RGGI tax and by reopening power plants, my administration will halt the skyrocketing utility electric bills and other market costs driving up costs of living including our grocery and electric bills.

But I need your urgent help today to fight and speak for you and win this election.
[](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=5aa292abeb&e=5bb5efcda7)
Will you help me with [your generous donation tonight](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=3907a10ff2&e=5bb5efcda7) to help our campaign reach voters? We have a little more than 60 days until mail-in balloting begins. I need your help today.

Thank you and God bless you and our State,
Dan Cox, Candidate for Governor of Maryland
About Dan Cox Dan Cox is a candidate for Maryland Governor and an attorney and public advocate focused on government accountability, constitutional governance, and consumer protection for Maryland citizens. Today I voted against SJM112...
It's a strongly worded letter to Congress asking them to please stop spending so much money (yes, the same Congress that hasn't balanced a budget in 25 years).
This is like sending a strongly worded letter to your alcoholic uncle asking him to please consider sobriety. He'll read it, nod, and crack another one open. Probably while telling you he's working on it.
$38 trillion in the hole... and we sent them a note.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Friends, I’m continuing the fight to defend birthright citizenship in the Supreme Court — and I want to share an update with you on where we are:
On day one of his second term, Trump signed an executive order attempting to toss out birthright citizenship.
I sued him within hours, and then we went on to repeatedly obtain nationwide injunctions by lower courts blocking Trump’s order from taking effect.
But Trump hasn’t given up the fight. So last week, I co-led a coalition of 24 attorneys general in filing an amicus brief in Trump v. Barbara, a case before the Supreme Court that was brought by a class of children who would lose their citizenship under Donald Trump’s order.
Let’s be clear about what’s at stake here if Trump’s unlawful executive order is allowed to stand: Hundreds of thousands of children born each year would be stripped of their ability to fully and fairly participate in our society as American citizens.
They would lose their most basic rights guaranteed by the Constitution.
They would be forced to live under threat of deportation, and some would be stateless, without a home country to return to.
Babies born here in the U.S. are rightful U.S. citizens — period.
The text of the Constitution and more than a century of legal precedent make clear that birthright citizenship is an American right, and Donald Trump can’t unilaterally undo that with unlawful executive action.
At the end of the day, every single branch of government, across administrations, has affirmed birthright citizenship — and that’s why I’m urging the Supreme Court to continue to uphold this right.
I will keep fighting to defend birthright citizenship and the rule of law, but taking on this administration takes resources. If you agree that every child born in this country is a rightful citizen, you can help support this critical work by chipping in to my re-election campaign today. We’re a nation of immigrants and California is a state of immigrants — including my own mom who came to California from the Philippines. Immigrants make our state and nation great, and I’ll always stand up for their rights and protections.
Thanks for standing with me.

| | | | | | **March 4, 2026**
This week, one of my Democratic primary opponents hired a MAGA lawyer who tried to overturn the 2020 election. Her lawsuit against our own Colorado Democratic Party would prevent people’s voices from being heard in caucus.**Let me be clear: we are absolutely continuing to go through caucus.** We are organizing. We are showing up. We are participating fully in the Democratic process in every corner of this district. No lawsuit, no political maneuvering, and no attempt to sideline all of us will stop us from engaging voters.We are not going to defeat Lauren Boebert by discouraging people from getting involved or playing dirty. This is why people hate politics. I served in the Navy for 34 years. I took an oath to the constitution. Despite that, one of my opponents has called me a “traitor” to this country and accused me of being a “Trump official” simply because I wore the uniform during his first term. That’s not just false - it’s the kind of toxic politics that drives good people away from public service. Our entire campaign is about including people. That’s why we’ve made more than 26,000 phone calls, held over 50 meet-and-greets, traveled over 13,000 miles, and recruited hundreds of first-time caucus goers.We win in November by engaging everyone and expanding our coalition – not hiring someone who already tried to overturn one election to suppress voters in another. To those who have already caucused for me: Thank you. To those who plan to support me in an upcoming caucus this month: Thank you. To those who are still not sure who they are supporting yet or those supporting another candidate: Thank you. Thank you for getting involved. Thank you for standing up for our community. We are going to win in November... But we can only do it together
---
| | \- Eileen

subject: They left us unprotected.

body:
**Friend,**
We are at war with Iran.
Our military is deployed overseas. The FBI is warning about heightened terrorism threats right here at home. And what are Democrats in Congress doing?
**They shut down the Department of Homeland Security.**
Not some obscure agency. Not a minor budget line. _Homeland Security._ The people who protect our airports. Our coastlines. Our cities.
## RIGHT NOW:
TSA agents are missing paychecks. Coast Guard training has been cut. FEMA can't process disaster relief. Secret Service reforms are frozen.
**And we are at war.**
My family knows what it means to live without protection.
In 1985, my father hid us in a fishing boat because the government that was supposed to protect us became the thing we needed protection from. We spent three days at sea. We spent 30 months in refugee camps. We came to America in 1987 because this country was supposed to be _different._
This country was supposed to keep people safe.
Democrats are gambling with that safety right now. They are holding homeland security hostage over a political fight — while American families, military families, communities like ours in Orange County are left exposed.
### Here's what they're playing politics with:
* **Airport security** — TSA workers can't pay their bills
* **Disaster response** — FEMA training centers shut down for 45,000 students per week
* **Coastal defense** — Coast Guard aircraft grounded
* **Cybersecurity** — critical deployments delayed

This isn't about policy disagreements. This is about basic responsibility. You don't defund your own security during wartime. Period.
I'm running for Congress because CA-45 deserves someone who will never play games with your family's safety. Not for political leverage. Not for headlines. Not ever.

clean_body: Friend, We are at war with Iran. Our military is deployed overseas. The FBI is warning about heightened terrorism threats right here at home. And what are Democrats in Congress doing? | Fellow Nebraska Republicans,
Your county convention and county party meeting is just around the corner -- and the Nebraska Republican Party (NEGOP) wants to make sure you're ready!
We've partnered with the Leadership Institute to offer a FREE Robert's Rules of Order training on Saturday, March 7th at 2:00 PM (CST). Whether you're a first-time attendee or a seasoned party member, this session will help you show up confident and prepared - all are welcome to attend.
Not familiar with Robert's Rules? No problem -- that's what this training is for. Robert's Rules of Order is the standard framework used to run meetings fairly and efficiently. It covers how motions are made, how debates are conducted, and how decisions are reached. Nearly every formal Republican meeting and convention runs on these rules, and knowing them means you can fully participate, speak up at the right time, and make your voice count.
In this free session, you'll learn how to:
✅ Follow along and participate at every stage of a meeting ✅ Make motions, join debates, and call for votes the right way ✅ Serve as a delegate or a presiding officer/chair ✅ Avoid the common mistakes that catch people off guard
Don't walk in unprepared -- this free training gives you everything you need to make a real impact.

## US Sub Torpedoes Iranian Warship
A U.S. Navy submarine torpedoed and sank the _IRIS Dena_ , one of Iran's most prized warships, in the Indian Ocean on Tuesday, the first U.S. torpedo sinking of an enemy vessel since World War II, Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine confirmed on Wednesday. [Watch the video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVui4zAmDAyVKm_pmtHC5ohpiYnMOWn69JX7Cl2_4fdJ_8t5OPuU03L98DdyHMuw0LNmYqZ12GrdRs_sp69ctrlk_gmJql8GBOwOoA6gh-BTfg1tE1wkQlINOWkMGrCAtpmdGQFCnCZDUWMbotZh0qdWK3-ysQPbJLdroEBLKQFPx1HFcbKtVMrD6KMRLVBIXNbjZ0kLzxTzqzxoPU7l1mQ3M9-rUG8Ce4H9974K7N_pziVe_Cqwr-x5qwJ7BLTSKqON7FAqazpsVhfuz5Rzqt3-dL35lP9k_leOh8PfAAAA___RK3Gq). Secretary of War Pete Hegseth called it a "quiet death" and said the U.S. is winning Operation Epic Fury "decisively, devastatingly and without mercy." On Wednesday, thousands of Kurds crossed from Iraq and launched a ground offensive in Iran. Now in its sixth day, the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign has hit nearly 2,000 targets inside Iran. [Follow live updates here.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOiNjc_goXKShu7Qp0YKXY5MFn-zlyOXrI_ILKUcjzdO8j9twA2La7u-wopc5DhsemVEE07DnvI8gAtMXx32JLD-BMMM2GG1apa3SlyEA8WtoyuBnRIO2RF87Z5zutOnKxbfg0NXBATSha7qLnSZtulYH64xrp2tJ_lzTVl_qutbmWo12Hqeuqa0FPcLsikZjIImp-oy0yYIzv-ITUzXFtWS_iDxyYd8K0xemP46jmuP3-eLsC9MzPVGduTD9nhUl2BTlBMjqgKQYBLOoFdK0qKZMPjwOYqbcnuD7CsR_IPmXnac3vwEAAP__7YF6XA) Iran's ballistic missile launches are down 86% from day one, and the U.S. expects complete control of Iranian airspace within days. Six American service members were killed in a March 1 drone attack in Kuwait; four have been identified.
## US and Ecuador Launch Operation Against Cartels
The U.S. and Ecuador [launched joint ground operations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAQhU8DHcgeA14KF2noNm1KNNjD4mTAKxgWkdNH7BXSPelJ3_v5uvd3jByXxyfO5GRM_ULHxiRCa79v2z6gCPofTvuUWH5DpA2XHhQ0hTKFqvuAkc--yoMbiYBMTk5bC1a1Ctp8cq2ucBgaY0dbBe0JQmhv4EeqB7iZEPLoLpoyqtZaK7iVgxkH31baGFQDjjarFIUoaS2_U1xkopHP9KK19GnO2U0izy0zHxl0GXTHcZQnTildbgbdNSeDDleJnumSe0F-x5DWgnFf_FS8qcUcOQquZ6Ft1dZgG1VOMnO-uvA8InPcmqvJY8bI72T5110vB38BAAD__6u3gD0) against narco-terrorist organizations this week, the first time American forces have participated in a ground mission inside Ecuador. U.S. Southern Command said American personnel served in an advisory capacity, providing planning and intelligence support while Ecuadorian soldiers conducted the operations. Ecuador has become one of the region's fastest-growing drug transit hubs, [sandwiched between](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u4yAQxfGnwZ2jYfDHuqDYxl223dIawxCzS4wF40S5T3-VvMKtj_TT0f_vdblSTHG__aE7Wwl52flZE4twWc5az5VEyP1P-dxyki8fudK-IODQgmmhXzzF9Fq6xtvAjGwatnoccYQJcGo226Ge9ECkmfvQawDdu3UNwQQwA62uifatgYFeaw3467KasLqp08YQrBRG1QH7KLlc_uW4y8YhvfKDy8Xle5PsJnJUZX4rnBXOsvEWU3pvCucjp-heCmfPgffKCud-HEYDQ3vWlt1JPpf2w7b54EIS815bR0U4VYVzU6w_njGlWIf3kdud4gdv5Ee1Hha_AwAA__-iRX-K) the world's two largest cocaine producers, Colombia and Peru, with drug seizures there nearly tripling since 2019.
## Notre Dame Coaching Legend Lou Holtz Dies
College football icon Lou Holtz passed away yesterday in Orlando, Florida, at the age of 89. He’s remembered by many as one of the greatest coaches in college football history, especially by [Notre Dame](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OozAUBeCngc6RfwiGwsU2dNl2S3Sxr_HdMTbCJhHz9KPkFaY_OufT-feYH0CR0voXNjTV5znhq0SsFY_5LOVcoFawXzGfIcf67QgLpFly2TOuGL_PDihec9c64xElqhaN0FpqPnI5tsE412vrBin6Ee5Db9Fp2TkAPywCnO5bMu82rvhdCMHlcFuUX-zYCaWAL-B103F0VPNx-58p1YA-XvmJx83mrY0m1LqXRv1p5NTIydMaKqWVDirhnWjkFPPJPnoWccXk4LhYgko5QWQ2wLZTTiXQzmwGG9gOpWBh8IKrkVN7GLe_KEYq_duybkDxs11_ddjTyJ8AAAD__-G_g1w) fans, where he coached for an 11-year span from 1986 to 1996. Holtz led six different programs to bowl games over a 33-year career (he’s still the only coach in NCAA history to do so) and finished with 249 career wins. His crown jewel, however, will always be the 1988 Notre Dame team that went 12-0 and [won the national championship](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkbHO2zAMhJ_G3hRIVGLZg4cu3v6uHQ1aomy2shVITIL06QsHKNC9CwkQd0d8uB9f8xdy4mP9jjuNEvN80KsmEqEyP2p9LCiC_lfKjy0n-R2YKh4zaOiUtkrf5oCc3vO1DWMkArItjcY5cHrQMLTb6EN0FgMNYEK36B4jdrerttaYRcMSWx7PNG31zRijob8sNi5-uBprUS8YXXPVFFhyufzMfMhGMb3zk8rF571N4yZyr4391sDUwBR53YSPlQvX7cWFLo-KkgO-T3kDU5Vc3ue-5yK1gcnnlGilf7zqYz4POcuCKTUwgQZoYNLdOVwD05GlkAq4k_orU2boe7Uz7qw8ypYT-6p8Pp7sP69c74y7GqM_CW0Zw_3FKXHtTsh1R04fKPmvJp4j_AkAAP__rcadfw), the program's last to date. After retiring from coaching in 2004, Holtz spent a decade as an analyst at ESPN, quickly becoming one of the sport's most recognizable personalities. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2008 and received the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdEZmzJpH4SKNu02bEhk8XpwMGNnDos3XR7tNPuDVR7o69_y6T3efKO2Pn35DyzFPO16VkBnLdNZ6zp7ZL38on2sm_hsSVr9PoMBIpaW6TcEnek19E2xEBNQN2m4YYFCjgrFZrVFgOoN-8UFr7EyPY3-bv_QMIywRTJPse01pdeu6TsFXO-s4L2Pfae3V7OMgeoUhcS7t75x2XjHSKz-xtEveGrIr81GF_iHACXDXdbVYj_0NBbglE-EDZcyZZ08kwFXO5SXATQJcCgKcVn2vx9EIcJRP-fkpCy6YnljlUbCmgDsnT3LD4EnGghjy9h_JkHdPQXI5t6MpNhxXIkrVvN0fm0_0ceVvBX5a-BcAAP__ZB2R2g) from President Trump in 2020. Holtz had been in hospice care at his Orlando home since February, surrounded by family. He is survived by four children, including son and fellow coach Skip Holtz. [See his career in images](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL8GMrmEhC0UKLiEzJdeSA1ohOZWIJc02MV-_Zb9C5t3dfd7_-7THSjRvv6FDR2HPO34qgmZsUxHrccMzLB8pXzEnPjbE1bYJyXVTUgt5HXyQOmc-ta7gKhQt-g6Y5SRVirbRhckzNYGO8zXYHqpJQyo0Qx-Ucp2ZmnJvduklteu66QaLrMO82L7TmuQMwTT9BI9cS6X_5l2jhjSmZ9YLkve2uQi86M2-k-jxkaNgdbItK9UqMZ3olHjI2bOYoWUsJwi5UN8WATHko81Co4oToRSBbDYMxcUHjZs1NgW5x8vSonq7f1j3YDSZ5d_Jevp1E8AAAD__xvSgOw).****

# Thursday, March 5, 2026
---|---
**Good Morning!** On [this day](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1ywyAQQOHToM4aWJCxCoo06pwiTUoGmZW8EwQaWP_dPuNcIeVrvuJ9n_05UKK8foYNHT-X4jM-WkJmrP5emPLaclhujett2xvmWGpDDxKOB6kPcvAxUHp500U3yziqDp2yFqwCdRq7qxtDtHqYhwWjHsYTmGjkOBsLaAatF-zIvTGp5aBAamn6-aLVBe0yno4gZxWFkRiJS-35iozP0Jb0Knes_aVsXXJX5r0J_SFgEjBh7h_0QztGCn2pq4Dp3QKmr5Djy58Dt5K76uL-oJSoHa0wct0CpT-P_3fh7uA3AAD__2dcck8) in 1945, shot putter [Randy Matson](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DvS2yAQAODToM6aZfXAKijSqHPalBrMLhIzCDywft0-k1zhv8BXfH9u283FFPP-251s5RPKlvndEotw3V5FYt5bduHZpD7PR-NMpTbeEHC-wHCBaSMX03cbO7J3oEV3bLUxaDTq69Id1qPzhoBm4yYdwkTLtIBBvAKhxtl30f7DYIBJIwww9nc_aM8mLNcZ4a5JjcAUpdReDhb-uBbSt7y49r6cXbKHyKOp4ZfCVeEq7SihL3VXuMZMTy_MCtfqMn0vp5NWssK1q5Ye75hSbLNRI-yni-m_Jz9beFn8GwAA__9CU3Hv) was born in Kilgore. A graduate of Texas A&M, he competed in the Olympics twice, winning silver in 1964 and gold in 1968. Matson was also drafted by the Atlanta Falcons and the Seattle SuperSonics, but he turned down both offers to focus on track and field. Today's edition continues our Election Day coverage, including confusion among some voters over [new rules](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O5CAQhJ_Gzhg1GPwTEFwy2V56oQVNM4OEjQU93p23P3leYcNSqUpV37-v9culnPbHX7eR5Z9Y1p2-WyZmqutZOO2Ptrv4alxf29FoD6U2WhWoUcAgwKzBpfxedR-sh7DInqycJjVJJeelf1oAA3LR6EdpHKDR0aM2iDhrQ4BDn-xVBgMYqWAAffM4SKQpLvOowMvQaaCQuNQbP4npx7WY3-WkesOy9dk-mY_WDX86de_U3R3Xgcu6ROWEmTp1_-TElgJT3Zo4C1Nt4ig5NxFoK1gdN1HpePmc0O1NmBidj0sY_QhBq6AjztovCGNYBke6rzYc3ynn1Map0_DYXMqfSfw7kKdV_wMAAP__ZwCJzw) in Dallas County and Williamson County. Share your opinion about where voters should cast their ballots in today's _Poll_ , and hit reply to let us know if you were affected by the changes. New voting procedures in Dallas County and Williamson County [caused confusion](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O5CAQhJ_Gzhg1GPwTEFwy2V56oQVNM4OEjQU93p23P3leYcNSqUpV37-v9culnPbHX7eR5Z9Y1p2-WyZmqutZOO2Ptrv4alxf29FoD6U2WhWoUcAgwKzBpfxedR-sh7DInqycJjVJJeelf1oAA3LR6EdpHKDR0aM2iDhrQ4BDn-xVBgMYqWAAffM4SKQpLvOowMvQaaCQuNQbP4npx7WY3-WkesOy9dk-mY_WDX86de_U3R3Xgcu6ROWEmTp1_-TElgJT3Zo4C1Nt4ig5NxFoK1gdN1HpePmc0O1NmBidj0sY_QhBq6AjztovCGNYBke6rzYc3ynn1Map0_DYXMqfSfw7kKdV_wMAAP__ZwCJzw) for some voters about where to cast their ballots, leading to delays at several polling locations. This year, in a purported effort to reduce election fraud, each county's Republican Party opted to require primary voters to cast their ballots [in their assigned precincts](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ_GdI78FwiFi9vQ5bZbImOPwVqDkT2Q8PYrR9on2Gak0Tn69M18PcenCTFs83-zgsa3T-MGrxIBEfJ4JgzbXDbjj4L5WPcCm0u5wCiYaCmTlN1HZ0K8RtU4PTHX8wY07zrRccEffbPoFqZe9e1dsOnRKdmrFjrPfauMNIzD1ARdYUyyOxdMMnWbrOQWOt8_WsEm7ohi4AKmfMMFEN6m-HilE_LNprWJekHcC5H_iBiIGMoOtrrGZE2st9QWEQO-a5gOXOiHQSHS3ZRExFBbRAxVg4iByd9xJoRc6JFncBQTtQvYb_paIENda0yTp3sOq8kXhQgWQ9qoM1eTtdtfIcZQ2o4oNq8mxI8v_u3LpxY_AQAA__97DpNA) on Election Day. In previous years, voters had been able to do so at any polling location in the county, but state law requires both major parties to agree to provide that option. Hundreds of voters were reportedly turned away from party-specific polling places in both counties, causing a "lot of infuriated voters," according to Dallas County election navigator Juston Marine. And just the other day, we rescued 8 families from the chaos and violence in Mexico. But our story goes much deeper than even that.
---

In 2022, we **deployed to Ukraine for nine months** during the invasion, **delivered medical aid to orphanages** , **supported 65 wounded veterans** , and **ran precision rescues and logistics.** And between 2023 and 2025, we **rescued trafficked children stateside** (including a 12-year-old trapped 45 days in California and a 16-year-old in Virginia), **aided persecuted Christians in China** , **responded to the Texas floods and hurricanes in North Carolina and Florida** , **evacuated 92 American families from Israel** during the 12-Day War, and provided aid after earthquakes and crises in Thailand, Burma, Cuba, Zambia, and more. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. body:
Easter is one of the most meaningful days of the year.

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zmb5g612vj6cmf0sgdvhfq1i2sq83u390go9uil8_rp22sh2s8i6epr2ctj6eoj4cph2bs)
---
Friend, Easter is one of the most meaningful days of the year. And for many of us, it’s also one of the easiest to rush through. If you’ve ever reached Easter Sunday feeling spiritually unprepared or wishing you had spent more time reflecting beforehand, I wanted to share something created with you in mind. [**_He Is Risen: 12 Scriptures to Prepare Your Heart for Easter_**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zf6gcv6rau4kpu8722ud522ilr97jhg0uj64dppo_rp22sh2s8i6epr2ctj6eoj4cph2bs) is a free devotional designed for the days leading up to Easter. It’s meant to be simple, steady, and grounding. Here’s what you’ll find inside:
---
* One full Scripture passage each day
* A short reflection to help you process what you’re reading
* A prayer to help you pause and respond

---
No long readings.
No heavy commitment.
Just a daily rhythm to help you approach Easter with clarity and intention. If you’re looking for a way to engage with Easter more thoughtfully this year, I hope this devotional serves you well. You can download your free copy here: [https://resources.preborn.com/he-is-risen](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zq1cjl89a9go0g910fdt4l24plfht3eo951d9ug0_rp22sh2s8i6epr2ctj6eoj4cph2bs) Wishing you a meaningful Easter season, Denise

body:
On Drawing Lines By Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI - With the 2026 midterm primaries already underway, the Supreme Court’s decision to issue..

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-february-5-12771814?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=5e699acab0&e=c16f400a56)
| | **On Drawing Lines **
**By Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI** With the 2026 midterm primaries already underway, the Supreme Court’s [decision to issue an emergency stay](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=65d095d279&e=c16f400a56) of a New York trial court’s redistricting order may prove to be one of the most consequential election law rulings of the cycle. (As a reminder that we told you so, we did [predict](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=f7b87da8b3&e=c16f400a56) some eventful shadow docket rulings in our first edition of the year.)The facts of the New York case are straightforward enough. A state trial judge ordered the redrawing of the 11th Congressional District, directing that its boundaries be configured to ensure certain minority voters could elect their preferred candidate. The order directed the state’s independent redistricting commission to produce a new map on an accelerated timeline, with primaries just months away. Congresswoman Malliotakis and others appealed and sought emergency stays with both of New York’s appellate courts. After neither acted, Malliotakis sought a stay from the Supreme Court who stepped in and said: not so fast.Justice Alito filed a [concurrence](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4cdf47552c&e=c16f400a56) defending the stay, while Justice Sotomayor authored a [dissent](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=47e6b292d2&e=c16f400a56) joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson. The _Purcell_ principle figured significantly in the Justices’ dialogue. Named for _Purcell v. Gonzalez_ , a 2006 Supreme Court decision, _Purcell_ holds that federal courts should avoid risking voter confusion by changing voting rules on the eve of an election. Sotomayor’s dissent argued that recent applications of the doctrine counseled restraint four months away from a primary election. Alito turned the argument on its head, noting that the purpose of _Purcell_ is to prevent disruptive uncertainty on the eve of an election, and therefore does not preclude the Court from “eliminat[ing] much of the uncertainty and confusion” a judicially mandated redraw would have caused, particularly one which “this Court would likely strike down if the cases reached [it] in time.”The implications extend well beyond New York. Indeed, as [NPR reported](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=eed20bdefe&e=c16f400a56), requests for Supreme Court intervention on redistricting issues have become “a recurring theme this term, a trend that is likely to grow.” The stay might give pause to lower court judges tempted to issue sweeping redistricting remedies on compressed timelines—at least where those remedies could turn out to be constitutionally suspect. State appellate courts should also be mindful that the Supreme Court was willing to intervene to essentially stay a state _trial_ court’s ruling after New York’s appellate courts failed to act. They cannot rely on avoiding Supreme Court review merely by sitting on stay requests to run out the clock. So, what about the substantive legal dimensions? Justice Alito’s concurrence framed the trial court’s order not merely as procedurally disruptive, but as flatly unconstitutional. Not mincing words, he lambasted the trial court’s remedy as “unadorned racial discrimination.” This framing is significant, and critics of this Court have not missed it. UCLA law professor Rick Hasen, writing at the [Election Law Blog](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2976afc215&e=c16f400a56), called the ruling's implications “ominous,” warning that Alito’s language attacking race-conscious districting is “bad news” for Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act—a provision whose fate the Court is currently mulling over in _Louisiana v. Callais_. Whether or not one shares Hasen’s alarm, the doctrinal stakes raised in Alito’s concurrence are real.The jury’s still out on the merits in New York. But the Court’s posture heading into 2026 is already coming into focus.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Alabama** Three people have been indicted for [tampering with 20 absentee ballots](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=956b39afd3&e=c16f400a56) in the Frisco City municipal election. The charges include unlawful use of absentee ballots and submitting false ballot applications. **Florida** Lawmakers in Tallahassee are expected to [pass legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=7b51f79ffc&e=c16f400a56) similar to the federal SAVE Act. This [legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=bcf6c60436&e=c16f400a56), among other things, would add documentary proof of citizenship requirement to vote in Florida elections. **Georgia** A PAC founded by Elon Musk was [reprimanded](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=7f98264aa8&e=c16f400a56) by the State Election Board for sending pre-filled absentee ballots to voters ahead of the 2024 election. **Indiana** Last week, Governor Braun signed bipartisan [legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=f1ac0dbd85&e=c16f400a56) [prohibiting ranked choice voting](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=c6933e5953&e=c16f400a56). **Maryland** A state compliance board [found that the Talbot County Board of Elections violated Maryland’s Open Meetings Act](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=6f3a13d268&e=c16f400a56) nine times over a 16-month period. One violation involved an uneven partisan distribution of election judges at a meeting leading up to the 2024 election. Others involved missing minutes, maintaining incomplete records of closed sessions, and failure to disclose reasons for closed session meetings.**Michigan** Counties are [divided over whether to offer early in-person voting](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=cc78914ea2&e=c16f400a56) in a special state Senate election for State Legislative District 35 that could determine control of the chamber. Only Democratic-leaning Saginaw County plans to provide early voting, while the two Republican-leaning counties in the district cite insufficient funding to do so. **New Jersey** A state legislative panel [advanced legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=28d4ff88a0&e=c16f400a56) which would grant state courts broad authority to remedy discriminatory election practices, including modifying election rules, redrawing voting districts, expanding governing bodies, and rescheduling elections when the original date would have disproportionately hindered members of a protected class from voting. The bill now needs to be considered by the full Assembly. The United States Postal Service has [completed its investigation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=67673ec207&e=c16f400a56) into the dumping of campaign mailers supporting Congressman Tom Kean Jr. during the 2024 election and referred the case to the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) for potential prosecution.**North Carolina** The Board of Elections [has begun working on upgrading the state's election systems](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=1fae4533eb&e=c16f400a56). As part of this initiative, State Auditor Boliek has assembled a new commission tasked with supporting efforts to upgrade the elections infrastructure. After a technical issue delayed the opening of Halifax County’s Littleton precinct on Election Day, the state board of elections [voted unanimously to extend voting by one hour](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=3a5b6194ad&e=c16f400a56). All ballots cast after 7:30 pm are treated as provisional ballots under state and federal law.**Texas** The state had an eventful day in its closely watched primary. There was considerable voter [confusion](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2612af4b81&e=c16f400a56) in Dallas County resulting from changes to how the local political parties administered the primary process. In short, the Dallas County Republican Party initiated a change that returned to a precinct-based voting system for election day instead of the normal countywide vote centers that were also used during early voting in the primary. Some voters, unaware of the changes, appeared at their usual vote center and were told they needed to vote at their assigned precinct. This also led to litigation which is discussed below in Court Watch.**Virginia** Early voting for Virginia’s April 21 redistricting referendum is scheduled to begin March 6 across the state. A [Tazewell County circuit court had previously halted](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=0b44dc79f6&e=c16f400a56) the county’s officials from preparing or administering the election as part of litigation challenging the legality of the referendum legislation. But the [Virginia Supreme Court has since stayed that order](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2184c481a9&e=c16f400a56), allowing election preparations and early voting to proceed.**Wisconsin** A new [bill](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2865c4f37d&e=c16f400a56) introduced in the legislature would automatically register residents to vote when they [interact](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=6690c5a48e&e=c16f400a56) with state Department of Transportation agencies.
---
|
---
| | **DOJ Voter Roll Cases** The United States Department of Justice has [filed five new lawsuits](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=274f2272f1&e=c16f400a56) against states (UT, NJ, KY, OK, WV) that have refused to provide their voter rolls to the Department. These new suits come just a day after the DOJ appealed rulings preventing the data transfer in Oregon, Michigan, and California. In total, the DOJ has filed suit against 29 states and the District of Columbia. **Alaska** _**Repeal Now v. Alaska Div. of Elections**_**, 3AN-26-04988СІ (Alaska Super. Ct., 3d Jud. Dist.)** On February 17, an activist group filed a [lawsuit](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=928f60024a&e=c16f400a56) challenging the [wording of a ballot measure](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=648c984047&e=c16f400a56) which would repeal open primaries and ranked choice voting elections. A similar measure was narrowly defeated in the 2024 election. **Arizona** _**Mi Familia Vota v. Fontes**_**, No. 2:22-cv-00509 (D. Ariz.)** On February 19, the [RNC](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=5516bf96f9&e=c16f400a56), [Arizona legislature](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=81f3937fb0&e=c16f400a56), and [State of Arizona](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4efcb2dd24&e=c16f400a56) each [filed writs of certiorari](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=d7ad33a849&e=c16f400a56) in the U.S. Supreme Court asking the Court to overturn the Ninth Circuit’s decision which partially voided Arizona’s documentary proof of citizen requirements._**United States v. Fontes**_**, No. 2:26-cv-00066 (D. (As a reminder that we told you so, we did some eventful shadow docket rulings in our first edition of the year.)The facts of the New York case are straightforward enough. A state trial judge ordered the redrawing of the 11th Congressional District, directing that its boundaries be configured to ensure certain minority voters could elect their preferred candidate. The order directed the state’s independent redistricting commission to produce a new map on an accelerated timeline, with primaries just months away. Congresswoman Malliotakis and others appealed and sought emergency stays with both of New York’s appellate courts. After neither acted, Malliotakis sought a stay from the Supreme Court who stepped in and said: not so fast.Justice Alito filed a defending the stay, while Justice Sotomayor authored a joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson. The Purcell principle figured significantly in the Justices’ dialogue. Named for Purcell v. Gonzalez , a 2006 Supreme Court decision, Purcell holds that federal courts should avoid risking voter confusion by changing voting rules on the eve of an election. Sotomayor’s dissent argued that recent applications of the doctrine counseled restraint four months away from a primary election. Alito turned the argument on its head, noting that the purpose of Purcell is to prevent disruptive uncertainty on the eve of an election, and therefore does not preclude the Court from “eliminat[ing] much of the uncertainty and confusion” a judicially mandated redraw would have caused, particularly one which “this Court would likely strike down if the cases reached [it] in time.”The implications extend well beyond New York. Indeed, as , requests for Supreme Court intervention on redistricting issues have become “a recurring theme this term, a trend that is likely to grow.” The stay might give pause to lower court judges tempted to issue sweeping redistricting remedies on compressed timelines—at least where those remedies could turn out to be constitutionally suspect. State appellate courts should also be mindful that the Supreme Court was willing to intervene to essentially stay a state trial court’s ruling after New York’s appellate courts failed to act. They cannot rely on avoiding Supreme Court review merely by sitting on stay requests to run out the clock. So, what about the substantive legal dimensions? Justice Alito’s concurrence framed the trial court’s order not merely as procedurally disruptive, but as flatly unconstitutional. Not mincing words, he lambasted the trial court’s remedy as “unadorned racial discrimination.” This framing is significant, and critics of this Court have not missed it. UCLA law professor Rick Hasen, writing at the , called the ruling's implications “ominous,” warning that Alito’s language attacking race-conscious districting is “bad news” for Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act—a provision whose fate the Court is currently mulling over in Louisiana v. Callais. Whether or not one shares Hasen’s alarm, the doctrinal stakes raised in Alito’s concurrence are real.The jury’s still out on the merits in New York. clean_body: This moment requires all of us to stand up and do everything we can. | Peter, The White House and their MAGA allies are doing everything in their power to undermine our democracy. We see it everywhere. We see it in their unprecedented gerrymandering efforts — ripping up maps in order to try to steer the midterm elections in their favor. We see it in their deliberately unconstitutional efforts to warp the census to undercount communities of color. We see it in their desperate efforts to commandeer state voter rolls and pass legislation like the so-called SAVE America Act, which would make it so much harder for millions of people to exercise their right to vote. None of this is an accident, Peter. And if they succeed in breaking our democracy in the months ahead, we may not get another chance to fix it.= | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = Over the last year, Republicans have made it abundantly clear that they are terrified of Americans coming out in droves to vote this November. They know that their policies are so deeply unpopular that simply holding a fair election puts their congressional seats at risk. They fear being held accountable by the will of the people. That’s why we see endless assaults on democracy, from trying to manipulate the census to their spree of radical mid-decade redistricting. We won’t let them get away with any of it. I’m so proud of the fight we’ve shown so far — our movement has thrown a wrench in their plans to cling to power. But they’re nowhere close to finished, so we can’t be either. = Thanks so much, Biz John Bisognano President, NDRC = = | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC. # **Condoleezza Rice urges Trump to "take care of Iran for good," praises Operation Epic Fury killing of Khamenei**
Former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice **[praised President Donald Trump's bold military action against Iran,](https://substack.com/redirect/60cfc2a7-f820-4db6-b36c-8ba2e77ce813?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** saying "Iran has been at war with us for at least 47 years" and noting that 75-80% of U.S. casualties in Iraq were due to Iranian-made roadside bombs. She argued the main objective should be to "render Iran essentially incapable of military action against us and against our allies," adding "if you can neuter Iran as a military power in the region, that's worthy."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60cfc2a7-f820-4db6-b36c-8ba2e77ce813?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **Why it matters:** Rice, who served as national security adviser and chief diplomat under President George W. Bush, referenced the 1979 Iranian hostage crisis and 1983 Beirut bombing that killed 241 Americans as examples of Iranian-led terror, saying "to say that this regime was not a threat ... it's ahistorical." She noted Iran has developed military capability to reach beyond its borders through terror proxies like Hezbollah and Hamas, which it arms and equips.
* **What she said:** Rice described American military action as "a series of events" dating to Oct. 7, 2023, when Iranian-backed Hamas killed over 1,200 people including 46 Americans, saying "I'm quite certain that October 7 with Hamas couldn't have happened without Iranian training and equipment and even maybe planning." She said the U.S. jumped on timing to "render them incapable" before Iran could strike back or rearm Hamas and Hezbollah, adding "taking care of Iranian military and nuclear capabilities is very important." Rice noted Iran's complicated demographics, with minorities suppressed by Tehran across "a population of over 90 million people on territory that's twice the size of Texas."

# **Pentagon identifies final two soldiers killed in Iran strikes: Chief Warrant Officer from California, Major from Iowa**
The Pentagon **[identified the last two of six U.S. soldiers killed](https://substack.com/redirect/3a658d6b-b5dc-4686-8a0a-3aafcd3e96b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** following strikes against Iran as Chief Warrant Officer 3 Robert Marzan, 54, of Sacramento, California, and Maj. Jeffrey O'Brien, 45, of Indianola, Iowa. Marzan "was at the scene when a drone strike hit the command center in Kuwait and is 'believed to be the individual who perished at the scene,'" according to the Pentagon.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0478a7da-5dbe-41e3-bb7f-5d081d679a8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Details:** The deaths bring the total U.S. casualties to six soldiers, all killed when Iran struck at least six U.S. military facilities around the Middle East since the U.S. and Israel began attacking Saturday, according to a New York Times analysis. Facilities in Bahrain, Iraq, the UAE, and three sites in Kuwait were hit Saturday and Sunday, with several structures including satellite communications equipment damaged or destroyed. President Trump warned the death toll will likely rise, saying "sadly, there will likely be more before it ends" as the conflict escalates over the next three to four weeks.
* **The other victims:** The four soldiers identified Tuesday were Capt. Cody A. Khork, 35, of Winter Haven, Florida; Sgt. 1st Class Noah L. Tietjens, 42, of Bellevue, Nebraska; Sgt. 1st Class Nicole M. Amor, 39, of White Bear Lake, Minnesota; and Sgt. Declan J. Coady, 20, of West Des Moines, Iowa. Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds said "our hearts are broken by the deaths of Major Jeffrey O'Brien and Sergeant Declan Coady, two brave Iowa soldiers who gave the ultimate sacrifice," while Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis expressed condolences for Capt. Khork, who "has been killed in the line of duty as part of Operation Epic Fury."

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller declared on Hannity Wednesday night that under President Trump's leadership, **[the U.S. military has been"unleashed" from political correctness after years of "woke"](https://substack.com/redirect/c6b438e3-2f6d-467f-a2f2-21da66e6e3a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** indoctrination under the Biden administration, where top brass "seemed more interested in pronoun etiquette than lethality and victory."

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: It’s official: I will be facing Greg Abbott this November
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
This win couldn’t have been possible without you, friend.

| | |
---
**It’s official,****friend****! AP called the race in the Texas Democratic Primary election, and I’ll be facing Greg Abbott this November.**
And now, we move into the next phase of this race with one mission in mind — defeating Greg Abbott and ending the era of corruption and negligence he has inflicted on Texas.

Thank you, friend. This wouldn’t have been possible without your support.
To every volunteer who knocked doors, every organizer who made the calls, every supporter who chipped in what they could, and every Texan who believed in this campaign early, thank you. You carried us over the first big hurdle and made it clear that Texans are ready to turn the page.

Now the general election is underway, and our mission is clear. We are going to defeat Greg Abbott and end the era of corruption and negligence he has inflicted on Texas.
**[If you’re ready to keep the pressure on and keep building momentum, will you pitch in $5 right now, split between Deb Haaland and my campaign, to help us start strong?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/6005?refcode=jtk400-bu-nd&t=1&akid=7979%2E400544%2ErVzDJ3)**
Politics was never the plan for me. But when they tried to close my son’s neighborhood school, I couldn’t just stand on the sidelines and do nothing about it — so I turned my anger into action and ran for the school board to change things. _And I won._ Since then, I’ve fought for Texas families alongside union teachers and parents of every political background because this is not about party. It is about putting our kids first.
**As the Democratic nominee for Governor, I will fight for Texans the same way I fight for my own kids,_with everything I’ve got._**
As Governor of Texas, I will work to build a state where:
* You can see a doctor without worrying that it will bankrupt your family.
* Your paycheck goes further at the grocery store and at the pharmacy.
* And make sure every child has a strong neighborhood public school, with supported teachers and safe classrooms.

After over a decade of Greg Abbott, Texans have watched the cost of living explode, public schools gutted and politicized, corruption run rampant, and millions denied health care. Texans are ready for something better.

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. Peter,

I’m incredibly humbled and honored to win my primary for North Carolina’s Fourth Congressional District. From the bottom of my heart, _thank you_.

The wave of support you exhibited for me and my campaign through a challenging primary has meant the world to me, and I can’t express my gratitude enough.

Despite all the challenges and curveballs we have faced over these last few months, your support is what carried us through to victory.

From millions of dollars in outside spending to false attacks against me and my record, you’ve stood by my side through all the obstacles we’ve faced. I am so grateful that this community saw through the outside noise and recognized the values I stand for, the work I do every day, and my commitment to representing this community with integrity.

So whether you helped knock on doors and make calls, contributed to our campaign, or mobilized your friends and family to get out the vote, your hard work has made a significant impact, and I am deeply appreciative of your support.

I am truly honored and humbled that the voters of this district have chosen to put their faith in me. Thank you for believing in me, supporting my campaign, and voting to uplift the common good.

I am eager to serve and continue to deliver for the people of the Fourth district and address the big challenges we face as a country.

With gratitude,
Valerie

name: Voter Action Project
subject: What went wrong in Texas on Tuesday
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NBC: Voting confusion in Texas rooted in conspiracy theories about ballot counting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=030526_1&amount=25]
Team: Voting was a mess in two separate counties in Texas for this week's primary election.
Generally, political parties in Texas oversee primary election voting. Democrats and Republicans often administer elections jointly and outsource the operations to county election officials, who have opted in recent years to have countywide voting centers that allow voters to cast ballots wherever is most convenient for them.
But Dallas and Williamson counties chose to run their primaries separately, at the precinct level. This led to mass confusion among voters of both parties about where they were supposed to vote.
In Dallas County, the confusion is rooted in election conspiracy theories about voting machines , which propelled the Dallas County GOP to abandon countywide voting in favor of precinct-level voting and led, according to some estimates, thousands of voters to show up at the wrong polling site.
This is what one kind of modern voter suppression looks like. Change the rules and locations, poorly inform voters, and soft-suppress anyone who doesn't have time to drive to multiple possible polling places because of work, or kids, or life. It's the type of suppression we've both warned about and fought against.
Our lives are hard enough, voting should be simple, secure, and easy. Help us fight for ballot access, ease of voting, mail-in ballots, and so much more with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=030526_1&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=030526_1&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=030526_1&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=030526_1&amount=50]

Voters in Dallas County used to be able to vote at any polling place in the county, which makes it easier for voters to cast a ballot on a lunch break from work or near their university. Not this year.
For example: Tomas Sanchez, a student at Dallas College, was among those who showed up at a voting location on campus to cast his ballot. He was told he was under a “mistaken impression” and that he needed to vote at his assigned precinct, a location about 6 miles away.
In addition, the Texas Secretary of State -- the state official responsible for running elections -- never updated their public-facing information on voting and precinct locations. So if you checked their official government website and lived in one of those two counties, you were told an incorrect location to cast your ballot .
Local political party offices got hundreds of calls asking where to go. Voters catalogued their issues on social media, from being told that a polling location was only for the other party (not theirs) to voters being told to go to another polling place only to be told to go back to the first location. Untold numbers of voters intended to cast a ballot and couldn't exercise their fundamental right to vote due to this sneaky suppression.

“The biggest divide in our country isn’t left versus right. It’s top versus bottom.”
#
We got some major news out of Texas this week, Peter.
James Talarico is officially the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate — and he's running on a message that's winning over Republicans, independents, and first-time voters alike:
**_“The biggest divide in our country isn't left versus right. It's top versus bottom.”_**
That message is landing in places Democrats haven't won in years. Because everyday people — regardless of how they voted in the past — know what it feels like when their wages stay the same while corporate elites get richer and richer. They know what it feels like to see the cost of living go up and up. They know the system has been rigged against working families, and they want someone who will finally say it out loud.
_James Talarico is that candidate._
He’s not running away from big ideas. He’s not playing it safe. James is running toward the voters that both parties have written off — and he’s speaking to their most direct concerns.

| Friend,
Defend Our Courts has been sounding the alarm about Trump's plot to rig elections since our founding in Spring 2025.
In our first major race, the '25 Pennsylvania Supreme Court election, we laid out the stakes for Democrats: Trump is attempting to take control of PA state Supreme Court so that he will have control over the court with final say on election related matters in the most important swing state in America.
In short, we've been warning that Trump is trying to control how states run their elections by planting his loyalist judges on State Supreme Courts.
Our critics called us "alarmist." MAGA called us crazy. But what Donald Trump announced proves without a doubt that the plot we have been warning about is very, very real:

Trump is now openly declaring his war on free and fair elections.
In the Constitution, it clearly outlines that state governments, not the federal government, have responsibility for how elections are administered. It's literally in the first Article of the Constitution.
And that means there's good news and bad news:
The good news: Trump's call to nationalize elections is so unconstitutional that even the MAGA controlled Supreme Court is unlikely to allow it.
The bad news: Now that Trump has publicly stated his end goal, MAGA's going to go nuclear to try and take control of state Supreme Courts across the country.
Defend Our Court's mission has never been more essential to preserving Democracy than it is now.
In 2026, there are state Supreme Court elections in several key swing states; Georgia, Michigan, and Wisconsin.
Last year, Defend Our Courts helped spearhead the defense of PA's state Supreme Court. And Democrats there didn't just win, they won massive 30+ point landslides. In Philadelphia where we concentrated the majority of our efforts, turnout surged by 34 percent. That was the largest increase in the state. And it made the difference.
Now we're taking our winning formula and our army of over 100k grassroots supporters to battle MAGA in GA, MI, and WI in 2026. With the national party stretched thin with House and Senate races, our role will be crucial in saving democracy.
