body:
This Lent, your faith can help protect the innocent.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvUm1OYVFxYXZrVg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNBQmxGNGI2RjA2ZW9scw/gaam0sw/s9m8bccec81)
| |
---
| |
---
| GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | Friend,
---
Lent is not just a season. It is a pilgrimage. A journey led by the Holy Spirit... into the desert. **And the desert is not empty.**
**It is sacred.**
**It is where God reminds us who we are.** When Jesus entered the desert, He was tempted. He was tested.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
But even then, one holy declaration still echoed from Heaven and did not change: **_“You are my beloved Son.”_** That same Father speaks over you. **You are His beloved son.**
**His beloved daughter.** Before any label.
Before any denomination. And so is every child. Even the child who has been lured... kidnapped... sold.
---
You may not know me yet. My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I produced the film _Sound of Freedom_ after meeting real-life rescuers who risk everything to save children from trafficking. **What I heard broke my heart.** Children treated like products.
Like profit.
Like they do not matter. I asked myself, _“What if it were my child?”_ That question changed my life. The film became a movement.
And the **Sound of Freedom Foundation was born.** But the story did not end when the credits rolled. Today, our foundation works to prevent trafficking before it begins. We **equip** trusted partners who rescue children.
We **educate** families so they can protect their sons and daughters.
We **advocate** for laws that defend the innocent. This is not politics.
It is protection.
**It is faith in action.**
---
[ Protect God’s Children Now ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
But if we are honest... Our hearts can grow numb and we get distracted. We get comfortable. **Lent is a wake-up call.** A time for metanoia.
A turning back to God. This Lenten season, pause and ask the Holy Spirit: “What do **You** want to restore in me?” Your prayer life?
Your courage?
Your tenderness toward the vulnerable? Because when hearts grow cold...children suffer. And today, many of God’s children are enslaved. **They are created in His image.**
**They belong to Him.**
**Their dignity is sacred.** When we forget that... the innocent pay the price.
---
[ Protect God’s Children Now ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
During Lent, I pray more intentionally. **I ask the Holy Spirit to strengthen us for this battle.** As a Catholic, I also ask for the prayers of the faithful who have gone before us. I ask **Our Lady of Guadalupe** to intercede for these little ones.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
I ask **Saint Joseph** to guard them.
I ask **Saint Michael** to defend them. Not instead of God. But asking them to pray with us... **as one family in Christ.**
Because this is spiritual warfare. **Light against darkness.** And Jesus was clear: _“Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.”_ (Matthew 25:40) When we protect a child, **we serve Christ.**
When we rescue the vulnerable, **we love Christ.** Friend, you may be hearing about this mission for the first time. But maybe this is not an accident. **Maybe the Holy Spirit is inviting you into something deeper this Lent.**
---
[ Protect God’s Children Now ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
**Let Him restore your heart.** And together, let us restore freedom to enslaved children of God. This is not about one church.
**It is about the Gospel.** **It is about the truth that every human life has dignity because it comes from God.** So we say it boldly: **God’s children are not for sale.** Not in our nation. Not in our world.
Not ever. Will you stand with us?
---
With gratitude and prayer,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)
---
Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation
---
[ Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e8256880/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS9zb3VuZC1vZi1mcmVlZG9tLWZvdW5kYXRpb24tMmExZDVlODctOGRhNy00N2ZmLTlkODUtZTJlYzEyYTZmZjE4L3RmX2ludHJv/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMDU/LbmNsd0VCSU43QQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlI4NzUyOQ/gaam0sw/s2u0343d6cb)

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMarch 5, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**Louisiana Public Service Commissioner Eric Skrmetta Endorses Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate**
**Baton Rouge, LA** \- Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow announced an endorsement from Louisiana Public Service Commissioner Eric Skrmetta in her Trump-endorsed campaign for the U.S. Senate, adding to the growing coalition of conservative leaders backing her campaign.
Commissioner Skrmetta, a longtime conservative leader and advocate for Louisiana ratepayers and energy producers, praised Rep. Letlow’s proven record and commitment to fighting for Louisiana families.
_“Julia Letlow has consistently demonstrated strong, principled leadership,”_ **said Commissioner Skrmetta**. _“She understands how critical affordable, reliable energy is to Louisiana’s economy, and she has never wavered in standing up to federal overreach. Louisiana needs a conservative fighter in the U.S. Senate, and I am proud to support her campaign.”_
_“I appreciate Commissioner Skrmetta’s endorsement,”_**said Rep. Letlow.**_“We share a commitment to supporting Louisiana families and protecting our state’s energy industry. I’m thankful for his support and look forward to continuing conversations about the issues that matter most to our state.”_
Rep. Letlow is the only candidate in the race endorsed by President Trump and continues to build broad support from conservative leaders across Louisiana. Her campaign for the U.S. Senate is focused on securing the border, unleashing American energy, defending life, strengthening education, and protecting Louisiana jobs.
For more information, visit [JuliaLetlow.com](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=990f9d2007&e=95355a072c).

**WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH** Women make history every day. This Women's History Month, we invite you to reflect, celebrate, and get inspired by the resilient, courageous women who came before us to build a long-term vision for our future.

In 2020, Virginia became the crucial 38th state to ratify the Equal Rights Amendment, and in 2026 Virginia saw its first woman Governor and Muslim woman Lt. Governor sworn in. Each step forward strengthens the foundation for future generations. We welcome more "firsts" here in Virginia until equality is a lived reality for all.
---
**AI USE IN EDUCATION BILLS ADVANCE THROUGH THE LEGISLATURE** We need to be looking at how our students are using Artificial Intelligence. It is clear that frequent AI usage has contributed to many of the struggles our students are currently facing, chipping away at our students' safety, critical thinking, and overall learning skills. These tools are advancing rapidly, and if we don't put some guardrails in, we will continue to see cognitive struggles amongst our youth.

Good morning, Peter —
First and foremost, I want to thank you for your support during the Democratic primary. A grassroots movement made up of people like you is the reason we were able to overcome tough odds to win the race.

Peter,

When the CEO of UnitedHealth Group came to Congress, Kim didn't hold back.

As a pediatrician for nearly 20 years—and someone who's lived with type 1 diabetes for decades—Kim knows what it's like to fight for care.

She hears the same frustration from families back home: people are _"pretty pissed off"_ at insurance companies because they're paying more and getting less.

Kim called out UnitedHealth for _"charging more, paying less, and then delaying or even denying care due to abusive demands for prior authorizations."_ She shared a story that should never happen: **a senior who had a stroke was told by their doctor they couldn't go home safely, but UnitedHealth refused to cover the hospital stay.**

**The result?**

A huge bill and a year-long fight to get care covered.

Kim called it _"unconscionable"_ and _"shameful,"_ and pressed the CEO directly, making one thing crystal clear: **their business model is built on wearing patients down rather than actually helping sick people.**

clean_body: Peter, When the CEO of UnitedHealth Group came to Congress, Kim didn't hold back. As a pediatrician for nearly 20 years—and someone who's lived with type 1 diabetes for decades—Kim knows what it's like to fight for care. She hears the same frustration from families back home: people are "pretty pissed off" at insurance companies because they're paying more and getting less. Kim called out UnitedHealth for "charging more, paying less, and then delaying or even denying care due to abusive demands for prior authorizations." She shared a story that should never happen: a senior who had a stroke was told by their doctor they couldn't go home safely, but UnitedHealth refused to cover the hospital stay. The result? A huge bill and a year-long fight to get care covered. Kim called it "unconscionable" and "shameful," and pressed the CEO directly, making one thing crystal clear: their business model is built on wearing patients down rather than actually helping sick | | | | | | I’ll get right to the point: the radical Left is perfectly fine with broken systems and rampant fraud as long as it keeps them in power.
Just look at what happened yesterday in the House Oversight Committee. Minnesota Governor Tim Walz (remember him?) had to testify under oath about the massive fraud scandals that flourished under his watch ... hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars stolen, whistleblowers ignored, and a complete lack of accountability.
We’ve seen the exact same disastrous playbook right here in Washington State. From the massive unemployment fraud that robbed taxpayers of hundreds of millions of dollars during the pandemic to the total lack of responsibility in Olympia, which squanders millions each year.
**If they won't even protect your tax dollars from blatant criminals, how can we trust them to protect the integrity of your vote?**
That is exactly why the House recently passed the SAVE Act. It is a piece of common-sense legislation that does one simple thing: it requires documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
Only American citizens should vote in American elections. It’s that simple.
**Here is exactly what the SAVE Act does:**
* **Requires Documentary Proof of Citizenship** : It mandates that anyone registering to vote in a federal election must provide physical proof that they are an American citizen, such as a U.S. passport or a birth certificate.
* **Forces States to Clean Up Voter Rolls** : It requires states to actively remove non-citizens from their existing voter registration lists.
* **Closes the Driver's License Loophole:** In places like Washington State, the radical Left proudly hands out driver's licenses to illegal immigrants. The SAVE Act ensures that a standard driver's license alone is no longer enough to get someone on a federal voter roll.

But now, the SAVE Act is sitting in the Senate, and the Left is fighting tooth and nail to kill it. They want open borders, they want unsecured voter rolls, and they want you to foot the bill for their failures.
**We cannot let them get away with it.** I am fighting on the front lines in Congress to secure our elections, demand accountability, and stop the fraud—whether it’s in Washington State, Minnesota, or anywhere else. But I cannot do it alone.
The radical Left is spending millions to unseat conservatives like me in 2026, and I need your help to keep the pressure on the Senate to pass the SAVE Act.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Trump’s Midnight Ultimatum - America is at a crossroads. body:
Today is day two of my general election campaign. I need you to keep the momentum going.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
As I head toward November as the Democratic nominee for Governor of Texas, I feel grateful for the grassroots support that has helped me get to this point and feel ready to take on the general election.
But I need to be honest: _the work ahead is massive._
That’s why I’m calling on you to become a part of the team as we kick off this race.
**[Will you chip in $5 to become a General Election Founding Donor today?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260305_1_foundingdonor.r3nnJD&refcode=em20260305-707&amount=5&t=1&akid=707%2E299639%2EfH-cFA)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260305_1_foundingdonor.r3nnJD&amount=5&refcode=em20260305-707&t=20&akid=707%2E299639%2EfH-cFA)
We’re up against Greg Abbott’s powerful political machines. He has billionaires, name recognition, and corruption on his side. He’s sitting on millions of cash, and is ready to spend it whatever way will help him hold onto power.
What he doesn’t have? **You.**
For more than a decade, Abbott has ignored Texans. They’re fed up with their tax dollars spent on voucher scams and tax breaks for the wealthy while healthcare, housing, and schools go ignored.
**And you all know that. You have lived it.**
This campaign is listening to Texans and giving them what they need. We have been around the state, holding town halls and answering questions. But what we still need is field organizers. Advertising funds to combat Abbott’s lies. The ability to put boots on the ground in all 254 counties.
That's where the Founding Donors come in — people willing to invest in this fight and help us build from the ground up.
**[I am asking you to be one of these people and contribute what you can.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260305_1_foundingdonor.9ZkUqZ&refcode=em20260305-707&t=21&akid=707%2E299639%2EfH-cFA)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260305_1_foundingdonor.r3nnJD&amount=5&refcode=em20260305-707&t=40&akid=707%2E299639%2EfH-cFA)
We have eight months to flip Texas. Let’s make every second count.
— Gina Hinojosa

[ Donate » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20260305-1&t=41&refcode2=707_299639_fH-cFA&akid=707%2E299639%2EfH-cFA)

A recent [Government Accountability Office (GAO) report](https://substack.com/redirect/f08e1f9a-e1e0-40a9-8ef6-51531e81f036?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) highlights significant fraud vulnerabilities in Biden-era humanitarian parole programs administered by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). These programs, introduced in 2022 and 2023, aimed to provide lawful pathways for certain noncitizens as alternatives to irregular migration across the southern border.

From May 2022 through September 2024, USCIS granted parole to approximately 774,000 individuals under these initiatives. However, the programs received thousands of fraudulent applications, exposing systemic weaknesses in fraud detection and internal controls.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.UFNyifBYbhkiX4oq2dQJPfwxAnBuQDU93sJxe3oUyvA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=188356807)
The GAO identified several critical issues:

Applicants submitted irrelevant or absurd evidence, including stock landscape photos and images of the U.S. flag, as supporting documentation.
The application systems lacked automated mechanisms to flag potential fraud, relying heavily on manual reviews that proved insufficient.

USCIS acknowledged gaps in vetting processes, which prioritized rapid processing over robust verification.

Critics, including immigration experts, described the design flaws as either malfeasant or inexcusably incompetent, noting that the scale of parole usage under the Biden administration far exceeded prior administrations' practices.

A USCIS spokesman defended the policies, stating they prioritized processing while maintaining security checks, but conceded the findings confirmed risks to public safety from fraudsters and criminals. The GAO recommended that USCIS develop comprehensive internal control plans to assess and mitigate fraud risks whenever launching new programs or modifying existing ones, including enhanced automation for detecting anomalies.

The report underscores ongoing challenges in balancing humanitarian relief with immigration system integrity, particularly amid record border encounters. It reveals how policy innovations intended to manage migration flows inadvertently created exploitable loopholes, allowing fraudulent claims to proliferate.

While parole grants provided temporary legal status and work authorization to hundreds of thousands, the influx of bogus applications eroded program credibility and strained resources.

This GAO assessment, released in late 2025, adds to longstanding congressional oversight of immigration benefit fraud, echoing prior reports on vulnerabilities in application processing and verification.

name: Tim Kaine
subject: Senate Republicans just blocked my Iran War Powers Resolution
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kaine for Virginia
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026]
I’m incredibly dismayed that the Senate has failed to pass my War Powers Resolution that would have stopped Donald Trump’s illegal and unnecessary war with Iran.
Let me be clear: This bill would not have prevented the U.S. from defending itself or Israel from an Iranian attack. And it said nothing that disputed Iran’s position as a bad actor — something we all agree on. All it did was ensure we do our constitutional duty to our service members and their families .
Yet every single Republican save one — my co-sponsor on this legislation, Senator Rand Paul — voted against it.
When we send service members into harm’s way, we absolutely must have clear objectives and a fully thought-through plan. Trump and his administration have neither — they have rushed into a war without thinking of the consequences on the American people and our economy, and on the stability of the entire Middle East.
Now, my colleagues’ failure to pass our bipartisan War Powers Resolution has added to a dangerous pattern of Congress relinquishing our constitutional duties to an increasingly erratic President.
How are we supposed to look our constituents in the eye — and send our sons and daughters into war — if we aren’t willing to take this most solemn responsibility seriously?
We have failed in our objective of stopping Trump’s dangerous and illegal war through this resolution. But we have gotten every single senator on the record. The 47 senators who voted for my War Powers Resolution have made a clear statement — and so have the 53 who voted against it.
I will not stop working to counter this President’s reckless maneuvers in every way I can.
I pray for the families whose loved ones will never come home. I pray this war will not turn into another endless conflict.
Thank you for your support,
Tim Kaine

"We love you. We support you."
Peter,

At Kentucky's Fairness Rally this week, Governor Andy Beshear stood before a crowd of LGBTQ+ Kentuckians and said these simple words: _**"We love you. We support you."**_

Andy has always been a champion for everyone's rights. His faith teaches him to love his neighbor, and he governs that way. He is the first Kentucky governor to attend the Fairness Rally to show support and love for Kentucky’s LGBTQ+ community — _and he has never missed one during his time in office._

When an extreme anti-trans bill reached Andy's desk in 2023, he vetoed it. He knew the backlash from Republican politicians would come. But he did it anyway, because it was the right thing to do. And when the LGBTQ+ community spoke out about the dangers of conversion therapy, Andy used his power as governor to ban it by executive order. Under his leadership, Kentucky’s state government proudly recognizes June as Pride Month.

Andy will keep standing his ground in support of every Kentuckian. At a time when LGBTQ+ people are under attack from Washington politicians, the need for leaders who will continue to stand up for the LGBTQ+ community grows stronger. [**We need more leaders like Andy who are willing to lead with compassion and integrity. ## **[Trump rolls on as Senate votes down partisan war powers act](https://substack.com/redirect/85aeb1f5-e782-411e-b224-97450e183152?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Senate **[voted down a war powers resolution](https://substack.com/redirect/85aeb1f5-e782-411e-b224-97450e183152?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Wednesday, giving President Trump unrestricted authority to continue military strikes against Iran after a US submarine sank an Iranian frigate in the first hostile sinking by an American sub since World War II.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/85aeb1f5-e782-411e-b224-97450e183152?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **War powers blocked:** The resolution failed as Republicans back Trump's aggressive posture.
* **First sub kill since WWII:** US Navy submarine torpedoed Iranian warship as the assault on Iranian Navy continues.
* **Iran vows revenge:** Tehran threatens to close the Strait of Hormuz and attack US assets.
* **Oil jumps sharply:** Brent crude surges 4.2 percent on fears of wider naval conflict.

### **[Iran war disrupts global travel industry](https://substack.com/redirect/cc13f232-ae2a-40da-88e4-1939551cbe05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Airlines, cruise lines, and hotels are **[seeing sharp cancellations](https://substack.com/redirect/cc13f232-ae2a-40da-88e4-1939551cbe05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and price swings as the escalating US-Iran conflict raises fears over airspace closures and safety in the Middle East and beyond.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cc13f232-ae2a-40da-88e4-1939551cbe05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Flights rerouted:** Major carriers are avoiding Iranian airspace and Gulf routes.
* **Cruise lines pause:** Several ships have been diverted from Persian Gulf ports.
* **Hotel bookings drop:** Dubai and regional luxury hotels see steep fall-off after rocket attacks on Gulf luxury playgrounds.
* **Insurance costs soar:** Travel insurance premiums spike 40 percent in affected zones.

# **[China sets record low GDP target](https://substack.com/redirect/2628d63b-d2a9-4655-99d2-8fe5d3781d43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Beijing announced its **[most pessimistic growth target in history](https://substack.com/redirect/2628d63b-d2a9-4655-99d2-8fe5d3781d43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at just 4.5 to 5 percent for 2026, admitting that deflation, US tariffs, and a collapsing property sector have severely damaged the world's second-largest economy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2628d63b-d2a9-4655-99d2-8fe5d3781d43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Lowest target ever:** China slashes GDP goal amid deflation and trade war pressure.
* **Exports under fire:** US tariffs and weak global demand crush Chinese manufacturing.
* **Power glut benefits miners:** Cheap electricity from overbuilt grids boosts crypto mining.
* **Global ripple effect:** Supply chains face fresh disruption as China struggles.

body:
It’s about the progress we’ve made together. |
#
---
Team, **Once again, Republicans have launched a new wave of attacks against me.** I’m not new to attacks like this, and I’m not backing down. But there’s only one reason why they keep attacking me: **They’re scared.** They’re coming after the progress we’ve made in Michigan because they know it stands in direct contrast to their extreme agenda. We’ve protected and expanded abortion rights. We’ve grown Michigan’s economy from the middle out and the bottom up — not just for the wealthy few. We’re fixing the damn roads. _And we’ve always put hardworking Michiganders first._ Our movement is strong, and our record is proof that progress is possible. That terrifies them, and it’s what national Republicans and their billionaire donors are desperate to undo. Since launching Fight Like Hell PAC, we’ve brought together a nationwide coalition fighting every day to stop Republican extremism. But as they double down on their attacks, this work is more urgent than ever. So let them spend their billionaire dollars. name: Adam Schiff
subject: Trump made himself a multibillionaire off the presidency
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=9605%2E5257348%2EE86mqH ]Adam Schiff for Senate

While you were struggling to afford groceries and health care, Trump cut a
secret $500 million crypto deal with foreign leaders to benefit himself
and his rich friends.

Asked about it in an Oval Office press conference, he said he doesn’t
recall it. I’m sure it’s easy to forget a half billion dollar payoff from
a foreign national just weeks before you are sworn in. Happens all the
time.

Maybe we should refresh his memory: a Gulf country sheik put $500 million
into the Trump family crypto business. His family got $187 million out of
that right off the bat, and the money is still coming in.

And this wasn’t just any sheik — he’s known as the Spy Sheik and is the
head of the UAE’s intelligence service, the brother of the UAE president,
and the manager of the UAE sovereign wealth fund. And his investment in
Trump’s crypto scheme has not only helped Trump become a multibillionaire,
but it has also paid dividends for the UAE, too.

They finally got their hands on some of the most sophisticated and
sensitive advanced American technology — semiconductor chips for AI. The
grift and corruption are as clear as day. So while Trump lines his
pockets, the UAE and other Gulf nations — which are investing in Trump’s
resorts, hotels, golf courses... and god knows what else — have Trump firmly
on their side. American policy is for sale to the highest bidder, and
they’re bidding billions for Trump’s favor.

Who’s left holding the bag? The American people.

We cannot lose our sense of shock and outrage over Trump’s bilking of the
American people and our national security interests to enrich himself. The
corruption we’re seeing right now is unprecedented.

There must be accountability, and if it doesn’t happen under this
administration — and it won’t — it has to happen when we seize control in
the midterms.

body:
We must pass the War Powers Resolution and put a stop to this illegal war.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260305-5972-footer&t=1&akid=5972%2E420207%2Ec_TOzV)
Peter,
Since Trump launched his war on Iran last weekend, millions of lives have been put at risk. Six U.S. servicemembers are dead, and over a thousand Iranian civilians have been killed, including at least 183 children.
If Trump isn’t stopped, this is just the beginning of the tragedy about to unfold.
**Let me be clear: Trump’s war on Iran is illegal, unconstitutional, and reckless.**
Congress _alone_ has the power to declare war. And yet, this president has decided to act unilaterally without any discussion, without any proof of an imminent threat, and without congressional approval.
It’s outrageous, disrespectful to the American people, and an egregious abuse of power that puts countless lives at risk.
After living through decades of endless wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, we’ve seen the human cost of conflicts like this. Lives are lost, families are torn apart, and taxpayer dollars go up in flames as defense contractors and CEOs get richer, and working people are told once again that there is money for bombs, but not healthcare or schools.
That’s why this week I’ll be voting **YES** on Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie’s War Powers Resolution to reassert Congress’ constitutional authority, rein in Trump’s abuse of power and demand an immediate end to this illegal war. **No president should be allowed to treat the Constitution like it’s a suggestion.**
[**If you’re as outraged as I am, please join me in adding your name to this petition to put a check on this president and put an end to this unconstitutional war before it goes any further.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/war-powers-resolution/?sourcecode=em20260305-5972&t=2&akid=5972%2E420207%2Ec_TOzV)

With gratitude,

* * *
Friend, You’ve probably seen headlines about Trump’s election chaos, court cases, and political fights. But what many Americans don’t realize is that Donald Trump isn’t just talking about changing elections — he’s executing a plan to do it. Since returning to power, Trump has repeatedly outlined an extreme vision for elections. Not through policy or debate, but through actions that undermine the system itself. So far, Trump has:
* Pressed for federal takeover of elections that the Constitution assigns to the states.
* Encouraged lawsuits and federal overreach into state voter rolls and administration.
* Undermined longstanding election security partnerships by weakening protections and cutting critical support for state and local election officials.
* Promoted conspiracy theories as justification for sweeping actions that would centralize control, not protect voters.

Friend, this a broader offensive on the core of American democracy, and it’s happening in plain sight. Our toolkit makes hosting your letter writing gathering simple 🧡 | | | Hi Peter, Are you meeting up with friends for cafecito this weekend? Or having a Bridgerton marathon? You can turn your next outing into an opportunity to build power and show solidarity to your neighbors in detention. Last month, over 115 of us came together at our “Powered by Love, Not Cages” community call to start writing letters to our neighbors in detention. Since then, more than 100 people have committed to bring their friends and family together to write their own letters. From New Mexico to Virginia, our communities are standing united to show our love and care to our neighbors in detention.****[**And now, you can grow our power by hosting your own letter writing gathering!**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpZ1zJK_sxAB20UoitlUG1Lm-LAdhazwvoA5xmriszHY9LgwrF8kjM_yWoGZI13e2A82bdjFKluNcgMst0tuZh2gejjw0bZttyHs5nOf7sV4yrh2uWRi4Yj-FfOtOBZygH8b18GK-gQm9RFVhnj0OnnJbdNxu3xbm_qv3Pz1WUnym8yGMlHVcKJy0ziqJVjgrffQpketlfuf8vHGu23BOuMmHDKfWCs0WXn6dOj_ozrr0/4oo/Ju1ec0ffQomGmTuY-8RNHw/h0/h001.7W5n6jkwfV0gjeYkof5uqg-vnSZiwYDgiZHpwh4TPUs) “Since I got to this Center all you will feel is sadness and mostly depression,” a 14-year-old child [wrote](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMQV6dbhoaBGh0vnghGdZEjKO5Hlx9SBl_UJE5W7y0HKeJzUSNBlHdFu-jBfNFH6JSkfKwUm1o1RCgybqmqxJdipwAcirCUaw6lrVkjCRtCK8tBgOK8YxNCrJeuWHblAmm04WXnDGLVmW7Q39WZikvhvdZyqp1Rcv4y3PqSIFmUge7X4cTm-5L6RAUh6mF-0nASKYwHx2J6qy7910laKkNjJEemAGwCxb8pdNgoTxY5wKUqQ7qWQpZfZvcpVFADL2FqM_eLo8GOlnJZRAinRtfUWacjVEuf3UuORkLt_3Ehx30_RcZgHZc77AEGWezKlyfgGO4gJl1a-gWpO_bJTUjp8/4oo/Ju1ec0ffQomGmTuY-8RNHw/h1/h001.sCjeFHlyGd3FKrV0IZa2fZtlGn1mqhFYudSZhTC6GNg) from within the ICE Dilley Facility. * **✍️ Best practices** to keep in mind as you start writing your letter

clean_body: Our toolkit makes hosting your letter writing gathering simple 🧡 | | | Hi Peter, Are you meeting up with friends for cafecito this weekend? Or having a Bridgerton marathon? You can turn your next outing into an opportunity to build power and show solidarity to your neighbors in detention. Last month, over 115 of us came together at our “Powered by Love, Not Cages” community call to start writing letters to our neighbors in detention. Since then, more than 100 people have committed to bring their friends and family together to write their own letters. From New Mexico to Virginia, our communities are standing united to show our love and care to our neighbors in detention.** “Since I got to this Center all you will feel is sadness and mostly depression,” a 14-year-old child from within the ICE Dilley Facility. In a moment where our neighbors are being separated from their communities, something as simple as a letter can offer hope, human connection, and understanding. We’ll be collaborating with local partners to get your letters delivered to our neighbors in detention. All you need is pen and paper to turn your next movie night or coffee date into a letter writing opportunity. 🤝 Can I count you in? 📸 Some of your neighbors have already started to send in their letters! Commit to hosting your own letter writing gathering today! When you sign up, one of our organizers will get in touch to provide 1:1 support and answer any questions you may have. You’ll also receive our exclusive Letter Writing Toolkit, with the following resources: ✍️ Best practices to keep in mind as you start writing your letter 🦺 Confidentiality and safety suggestions to protect you, your loved ones, and our neighbors in detention 📬 Instructions on how to deliver your letters to our P.O. Box. We’ll take it from there, and partner with local organizations to send your letters to our neighbors in detention. 💌 I**deas on how to invite your friends to your gathering, including some cute text messages and social media samples. Peter, every letter is a reminder to our neighbors in detention that they are not alone — and that our community on the outside is fighting for their safety and dignity. 💌 In unity, Ximena and the UWD team | Follow us on: | | | | |

_**by Ellie Leonard, Blue Amp Media Contributing Editor**_
In the history of the Trump Administration and the Epstein Files we've often talked about leaks, spies, moles, the idea of someone on the inside funneling valuable information to the American public that would otherwise be hidden behind corruption and bureaucracy, not unlike the Tuskegee Syphilis Study, the Iran Contra Affair, or the Watergate Scandal. We think of heroes like Miles Taylor, who risked his reputation and the safety of his family to write the anonymous New York Times op-ed _[I Am Part of the Resistance Inside the Trump Administration](https://substack.com/redirect/4f1e2d2f-e22c-46b0-80a0-568feff424db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_, chronicling the cabinet's attempts at restraining an unhinged world leader _._
> #### "There is literally no telling whether he might change his mind from one minute to the next." \- Anonymous top official inside the White House
We think of Daniel Ellsberg who leaked the Pentagon Papers in 1971, which proved the U.S. government had misled the American public about the Vietnam War.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Donald Trump revoked Taylor's security clearance and accused him of treason. Ellsberg was charged under the Espionage Act of 1917. However, neither man was ultimately convicted of a crime.
But what if we had someone leaking information the other direction, taking it from the American public and funneling it back to powerful people to use as a means to stifle scandals and benefit the men behind the curtain? Or what if someone acted as both? What if there was someone investigating the powers that be, writing books and articles that seemed to reveal decades of deals with the devil, but also playing a few hands themselves? How dangerous would a double agent in the Epstein Files be?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Monocle Radio
I started following Michael Wolff a couple years ago, when I didn't know much about Epstein but knew Wolff had made it his life's works to infiltrate the "eye of the most extraordinary political storm since at least Watergate." And thus, beginning sometime in January 2017, he did just that, becoming renowned for being the journalist who, second to Maggie Haberman, had the most unfettered access to Donald Trump. It led to the publication of his most notable book, _Fire and Fury: Inside the Trump White House_ , which debuted at #1 on the New York Times Best Seller list, selling nearly 5 million copies worldwide and making Wolff a millionaire.
But I don't think that's why I paid attention. Because despite my greenhorn status in the political world, I'd heard rumors of interview tapes, about 100 hours of them, talking to a man who knew everything, knew every _one_ , and had potentially led one of the biggest crime rings in American history.
His name was Jeffrey Epstein.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
At the time, I had a little transcription business (still do), and the idea of listening to interviews this far off the record felt kind of delicious. Up until that point I'd spent most of my late nights listening to interviews with Woody Allen, Mia Farrow, Michelle and Barack Obama, Harry and Meghan, and a long list of survivors who still have not gone on the record to name their attackers in the White House, Hollywood, the music industry, and abroad. I've signed endless NDAs and know things Oprah wishes she did. All from my little second-hand couch in western Montana, one or two kids (at the time) still on the breast, and just trying to pay rent.
Now I'm known as the "Epstein Girl," a title which I hope to shake here in the near future as this investigation winds down and I can reclaim my writing skills on more than one topic. But for now, it means paying attention. And 3.5 million files later, it appears the sleep deprivation is paying off.
I wrote a piece about Michael Wolff just after Christmas. I'd read through all of his emails with Epstein from the November 12th file drop, that started innocently enough. He wanted to write a book about the disgraced financier, potentially in the same way he wanted to write about Trump--an expose of a bad guy in power who was willing to say and do anything for headlines. And sure, Wolff had been a little vague about _whose_ idea it was to write the book, seeming to claim that Epstein had pushed him to do it. So he bluffed a little. I could look past it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Guardian
But as I read pages and pages of emails between Epstein and Wolff, organizing them into a long, chronological thread over years, I started to realize this wasn't a business proposition; it was a friendship. And the same type of friendship Epstein had with most people--you give me something, I'll give you something; you screw with me, and your reputation is effectively over.
It started with a flight sometime between 1999-2001, when Wolff traveled on Epstein's plane to the West Coast for a TED conference. He noticed something off, a group of teenagers that never left Epstein's side.
> #### "You didn't know what to make of this...Who is this man with this very large airplane and these very tall girls?" \- Michael Wolff
But it didn't bother him much, because in 2004 Wolff joined Mort Zuckerman, Epstein, Harvey Weinstein, Donny Deutsch, and Nelson Peltz in an attempt to buy New York Magazine, which eventually fell through.
Fast forward to January 30th, 2026, when the Department of Justice released 3.5 million newly-public files from the Epstein case, including 1,830 pages of emails between Michael Wolff and Jeffrey Epstein. In their conversations, which now appeared to start much earlier, Wolff traveled to meet Epstein all over the world, interviewing him, bringing his family, even discussing visiting Epstein's island in the Caribbean.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Wolff often came to the house for dinners with Epstein and Woody Allen, where they discussed the backlash of the MeToo Movement and how to counter it and dodge the accusations that had chased down most of their friends. They often talked about Ronan Farrow's championing of his sister Dylan, and disparaged Nick Kristoff for allowing her to tell the story of her abuse and abuser in his New York Times [blog](https://substack.com/redirect/c2ddc8f8-5bc8-48d5-af11-b865762caa41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But even prior to the MeToo Movement, things seemed to take a turn in their relationship, and it was no longer about ignoring or joking about Epstein's past, but now campaigning for Epstein's revamped image. As early as 2011, Wolff was talking about discrediting other journalists who tried to tell the truth about Epstein's criminal history, both financially and in the sexual trafficking of young girls.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2015, Wolff was slated to write a piece on Epstein for New York Magazine, including the now well-known photographs from Christopher Anderson that were recently published on Instagram. However, at some point Epstein backed out, ghosting the magazine and Wolff as well, despite their close relationship. Or so it seemed. The magazine's photo team turned to Wolff to see if they could find Epstein for final publication, but Wolff was no help.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
> #### "Dear Michael, I hope this message finds you well. Know that we have been trying to reach Jeffrey via email, but he is not responding." \- Jody Quon, NYM Photo Editor
Wolff claimed he was trying to reach Epstein, but "obviously can't do more than that." Meanwhile, he'd sent the whole email thread to Epstein for review.
> #### "Let me know what you want to do about this. Cold in Paris." \- Michael Wolff
The article was never published, and the photographs wouldn't be made public until six years after Epstein's death.
In early 2016, Wolff got word that James Patterson was writing a book about Epstein. He approached the publisher, asking if he could read an advanced copy. This is his conversation with Erinn McGrath of Little, Brown and Company.
_**March 16, 2016**_
_**Erinn:** Hi Michael, so sorry for the delay - I was out of the office until this morning. We'll be publishing the book in August. Would love to set up an interview with you and Jim sometime before then - and [REDACTED] happy to share an early copy once we have those available._
_**Michael:** When do you think you'll have copies?_
_**Erinn:** In the next month or so I hope!_
_**Michael:** Keep me posted. Would appreciate it._
_**Erinn:** Will do!_
_**August 1, 2016**_
_**Michael:** Any chance you have galleys yet or [a manuscript] you're showing? Best, Michael._
_**August 2, 2016**_
_**Erinn:** Yes! We can pass along a copy so long as you're able to sign a NDA_
_**Michael:** That's no problem. Do you want to send me the NDA? And when is official pub date now?_
_**Erinn:** Gabby, cc'ed can get you the NDA! The new pub date is 10/10_
_**Michael:** Great. Thanks. m_
_**August 3, 2016**_
_**Erinn:** Thanks for signing this NDA, Michael -- we will let you know once we're able to send you a copy of the manuscript._
#### **After signing the NDA, Wolff forwarded all the correspondence about the book to Epstein**
Michael Wolff continued to correspond with Epstein on the regular until he died, but during that time, and especially after his entry into the White House, Wolff seemed to wield more power when it came to information. And Epstein knew it. Not only were they discussing the information coming _out_ of the Trump Administration, but at some point Epstein, with Wolff's knowledge, began sending ideas and letters back _to_ the White House, including during the Mueller Investigation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I don't know what was sent by Epstein, or if it ever ended up on Bill Barr's desk. I don't know if there was ever a leak. But Michael Wolff knows, and two weeks later Robert Mueller would conclude the Russia probe.
I've followed Michael Wolff, including a paid subscription, purchasing two books, and feverishly watching all of his interviews (and enjoying the decor) for a very long time. But the analytical side of me can't ignore the complicated relationship he had with Jeffrey Epstein that included changing the narrative, quashing stories, discrediting journalists, and, for all intents and purposes, hiding 100 hours of interviews that could help bring this investigation to a conclusion and give justice to over a thousand survivors. I'm not saying it has all the answers, but 100 hours with a criminal mastermind, a global financial mob boss, a sex-trafficking kingpin, wouldn't lead us to nothing.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6a1795b7-63b8-4441-a375-b0596902e02d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But also, considering how Wolff played two sides of the coin with Jeffrey Epstein and the American public who revered him, what do we know about the relationship he's had with Donald Trump? How did he get as much information as he did, and what did Trump get in return? It's just conjecture, but it's an honest question that needs honest answers. I've lost my faith in the integrity of Wolff's writing, and more importantly, his intent. Would Melania Trump really sue the man they let into the White House again and again for long and very willing conversations? And considering Wolff's overt protection of Epstein, has he protected Trump, too, in this investigation? After all, it was Epstein who knew everything about Donald Trump, and who was willing to talk about it. And I'll bet that's just what he did in those interviews.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72add344-d80f-43b8-9220-63493ef9ae2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But we don't have the interviews. We don't have the transcripts. And my belief is it's because Wolff now knows they would not only condemn Epstein, but they'd condemn Trump, and probably Wolff, too. Otherwise, why wouldn't he release them, all 100 hours of conversations with a man he called a "Monster?"
After all, who doesn't want to catch a monster?
> #### "For almost very one of his friends he would sooner or later urge them to see their financial lives in highly personal fashion. In part, this was the root of his relationship with wealthy men, to help them see their wealth as a living, emoting, vital part of themselves. Your fortune reflected your life. Your life reflected your fortune. Own it." \- Michael Wolf, _Too Famous._

They often talked about Ronan Farrow's championing of his sister Dylan, and disparaged Nick Kristoff for allowing her to tell the story of her abuse and abuser in his New York Times . | | ---|---|--- But even prior to the MeToo Movement, things seemed to take a turn in their relationship, and it was no longer about ignoring or joking about Epstein's past, but now campaigning for Epstein's revamped image. As early as 2011, Wolff was talking about discrediting other journalists who tried to tell the truth about Epstein's criminal history, both financially and in the sexual trafficking of young girls. | | ---|---|--- In 2015, Wolff was slated to write a piece on Epstein for New York Magazine, including the now well-known photographs from Christopher Anderson that were recently published on Instagram. However, at some point Epstein backed out, ghosting the magazine and Wolff as well, despite their close relationship. Or so it seemed. The magazine's photo team turned to Wolff to see if they could find Epstein for final publication, but Wolff was no help. | | ---|---|--- #### "Dear Michael, I hope this message finds you well. Know that we have been trying to reach Jeffrey via email, but he is not responding." \- Jody Quon, NYM Photo Editor Wolff claimed he was trying to reach Epstein, but "obviously can't do more than that." Meanwhile, he'd sent the whole email thread to Epstein for review. #### "Let me know what you want to do about this. Cold in Paris." \- Michael Wolff The article was never published, and the photographs wouldn't be made public until six years after Epstein's death. In early 2016, Wolff got word that James Patterson was writing a book about Epstein. He approached the publisher, asking if he could read an advanced copy. This is his conversation with Erinn McGrath of Little, Brown and Company. March 16, 2016 Erinn: Hi Michael, so sorry for the delay - I was out of the office until this morning. We'll be publishing the book in August. Would love to set up an interview with you and Jim sometime before then - and [REDACTED] happy to share an early copy once we have those available. Michael: When do you think you'll have copies? Erinn: In the next month or so I hope! Michael: Keep me posted. Would appreciate it. Erinn: Will do! August 1, 2016 Michael: Any chance you have galleys yet or [a manuscript] you're showing? Best, Michael. August 2, 2016 Erinn: Yes! We can pass along a copy so long as you're able to sign a NDA Michael: That's no problem. Do you want to send me the NDA? And when is official pub date now? Erinn: Gabby, cc'ed can get you the NDA! The new pub date is 10/10 Michael: Great. Thanks. m August 3, 2016 Erinn: Thanks for signing this NDA, Michael -- we will let you know once we're able to send you a copy of the manuscript. After signing the NDA, Wolff forwarded all the correspondence about the book to Epstein** Michael Wolff continued to correspond with Epstein on the regular until he died, but during that time, and especially after his entry into the White House, Wolff seemed to wield more power when it came to information. And Epstein knew it. Not only were they discussing the information coming out of the Trump Administration, but at some point Epstein, with Wolff's knowledge, began sending ideas and letters back to the White House, including during the Mueller Investigation. | | ---|---|--- I don't know what was sent by Epstein, or if it ever ended up on Bill Barr's desk. I don't know if there was ever a leak. But Michael Wolff knows, and two weeks later Robert Mueller would conclude the Russia probe. I've followed Michael Wolff, including a paid subscription, purchasing two books, and feverishly watching all of his interviews (and enjoying the decor) for a very long time. But the analytical side of me can't ignore the complicated relationship he had with Jeffrey Epstein that included changing the narrative, quashing stories, discrediting journalists, and, for all intents and purposes, hiding 100 hours of interviews that could help bring this investigation to a conclusion and give justice to over a thousand survivors. I'm not saying it has all the answers, but 100 hours with a criminal mastermind, a global financial mob boss, a sex-trafficking kingpin, wouldn't lead us to nothing. But also, considering how Wolff played two sides of the coin with Jeffrey Epstein and the American public who revered him, what do we know about the relationship he's had with Donald Trump? How did he get as much information as he did, and what did Trump get in return? It's just conjecture, but it's an honest question that needs honest answers. I've lost my faith in the integrity of Wolff's writing, and more importantly, his intent. Would Melania Trump really sue the man they let into the White House again and again for long and very willing conversations? And considering Wolff's overt protection of Epstein, has he protected Trump, too, in this investigation? After all, it was Epstein who knew everything about Donald Trump, and who was willing to talk about it. And I'll bet that's just what he did in those interviews. | | ---|---|--- But we don't have the interviews. We don't have the transcripts. And my belief is it's because Wolff now knows they would not only condemn Epstein, but they'd condemn Trump, and probably Wolff, too. Otherwise, why wouldn't he release them, all 100 hours of conversations with a man he called a "Monster?" After all, who doesn't want to catch a monster? #### "For almost very one of his friends he would sooner or later urge them to see their financial lives in highly personal fashion. In part, this was the root of his relationship with wealthy men, to help them see their wealth as a living, emoting, vital part of themselves. Your fortune reflected your life. Your life reflected your fortune. Own it." \- Michael Wolf, Too Famous. You're currently a free subscriber to . | | | | | | Peter,
---
| | Thank you for signing the Prioritize Humanity Pledge!
In a time when cruelty is normalized and division is weaponized, you made a different choice. You chose dignity. You chose accountability. You chose to say that leadership must begin — and end — with humanity.
That matters.
But movements don’t grow because of one signature. **They grow because people invite others in.**
If this pledge reflects your values, chances are it reflects the values of others in your life, too — your friends, your family, your coworkers, your community. The more names we add, the stronger our collective voice becomes when we demand better from candidates and elected officials.
Forward the pledge.Make posts on social media.Text it to three people who care about justice and human rights.
**When leaders see thousands standing behind a shared commitment to dignity and civil rights, they pay attention.**
We are building a visible, undeniable standard for leadership in this country — and you’re now part of that foundation.
Let’s keep growing.

And they're saying I stand **NO CHANCE** in my race for Governor.

Right now, the stakes couldn't be higher, and MAGA is being backed into a wall.

I'm holding the line, but I can't do it alone. Florida is the backbone of MAGA, which is why my race has become the _**MOST-TARGETED**_ race in the country.

I'm personally asking every single patriot reading this message to step up, right here, right now, and help me deliver a CRUCIAL victory for MAGA.

This is the moment where silence could result in the worst thing possible.

So I have to ask you directly: can I count on you?

name: Tim Walz
subject: How authoritarian politics work
body:
Peter,
When I demanded transparency and accountability for what’s happening in Minnesota, the Department of Justice turned its attention to me.
That’s not a coincidence. It’s retaliation.
This is how authoritarian politics work: overwhelm your critics, weaponize the justice system, and make the cost of speaking up so high that people stop doing it.
I won’t stop, because Minnesota believes in the rule of law. We believe in dignity. We believe real public safety comes from trust and cooperation — not fear, chaos, or political theater.
But fighting back against this kind of retaliation is expensive by design. And that’s why I’m asking for your help.
If you’re able, please contribute $25 to our Legal Defense Fund and Outrage then Action today so we can keep standing up for Minnesotans, defending the rule of law, and pushing back against this abuse of power. If yesterday is any indication, hundreds more GOP members of the House are going to fall in line when they vote for Trump’s war today. Cowards. Every single one of them.
#
Peter — yesterday, every Republican Senator (with the exception of Rand Paul) voted for Trump’s war.
They voted to cede their power to declare war — power granted to them by the Constitution — to Donald Trump. | Good afternoon Friend,
We are often told that the future of energy is already decided. Oil and gas, they say, must give way. Net zero is inevitable. Electric vehicles will soon replace combustion engines. Wind and solar must dominate. But what does this actually mean for states like Mississippi? How do we maintain our competitive edge? How do we protect the affordable, reliable energy that has helped attract billions in investment to our state? On March 19, the 5th Viscount Ridley — commonly known as **Matt Ridley** — will be in Jackson for an exclusive luncheon to address these very questions.

A close friend of U.S. Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** , he has been deeply engaged in conversations shaping energy policy on both sides of the Atlantic. Places at this exclusive lunch are limited. If you would like to hear one of the world’s leading voices on energy policy — and be in the room with others shaping Mississippi’s future — please reserve your seat today.

Colorado’s most valuable company leaves—Weeks after protests outside its Denver office
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A [former state senator was convicted on four felony counts](https://link.email.joinrmv.) tied to forged letters submitted during a legislative ethics investigation, receiving probation, community service, and a fine. A follow-up analysis notes the [same felony statute led to a far harsher outcome](https://link.email.joinrmv.) for former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters, who received a prison sentence nearing nine years—raising debate over sentencing disparities.

Palantir moved its headquarters to Miami, creating concerns about the [economic impact of it's exit](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Denver [approved a ban on masked officers](https://link.email.joinrmv.) during arrests and limits on federal immigration enforcement, while also becoming a finalist to host the [2028 Democratic National Convention](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Meanwhile, ranchers warn [wolf reintroduction is increasing conflicts](https://link.email.joinrmv.), tensions over furbearer hunting prompted [added security at a wildlife meeting](https://link.email.joinrmv.), and commentary questions climate headlines after warnings about [low snowpack collided with forecasts for heavy snowfall](https://link.email.joinrmv.).
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Commentary argues recent U.S. strikes on Iran reflect a [strategy of American strength](https://link.email.joinrmv.) aimed at stopping the regime from reaching nuclear capability and threatening global energy routes. Another analysis suggests the upheaval following the strikes [could mark a turning point](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Meanwhile, the Supreme Court sided with parents [challenging California gender-identity secrecy policies](https://link.email.joinrmv.), and a Senate panel will examine [limits on birthright citizenship](https://link.email.joinrmv.).
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, March 5, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado’s most valuable company leaves—Weeks after protests outside its Denver office](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
On February 17, Palantir Technologies posted a single sentence on X: “We have moved our headquarters to Miami, Florida.”
There was no press conference and no detailed explanation.
At the time of the move, Palantir was the most valuable publicly traded company headquartered in Colorado, with a market capitalization in the tens of billions of dollars. And just like that, the state’s highest-valued corporate name had a new address.
The announcement was brief. The consequences may not be.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**[Two Cases, One Law: Forged Letters, Election Controversy, and Colorado’s Sentencing Divide](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE [PART 1](https://link.email.joinrmv.) & [PART 2](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Forged letters end a lawmaker’s career:** Former Colorado Sen. Sonya Jaquez Lewis was convicted on four felony counts after submitting forged letters during a Senate ethics investigation, a breach of trust that prosecutors said was intended to influence the outcome of the inquiry.
* **Same felony statute, drastically different sentence:** Despite the serious convictions, the Denver court imposed probation, community service, and a fine, highlighting how Colorado’s “attempting to influence a public servant” statute allows wide judicial discretion in sentencing.
* **[Comparison with Tina Peters fuels political debate:](https://link.email.joinrmv.) **The case gained new attention because the same statute was used to prosecute former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters, who received a prison sentence nearing nine years, sparking ongoing debate over fairness, judicial discretion, and political context in Colorado’s justice system.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|

|
---
**[Why Iran Matters to Every Single American](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY HEIDI GANHAL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Iran’s nuclear clock is ticking:** Iranian leaders recently boasted that their enriched uranium stockpile could produce multiple nuclear weapons, raising fears that a regime openly hostile to the U.S. could soon cross the nuclear threshold.
* **The Strait of Hormuz affects every American:** Roughly 20% of the world’s oil passes through the narrow waterway Iran has threatened to close, meaning conflict in the region could quickly hit Americans through higher gas prices, supply chain disruptions, and global economic instability.
* **Deterrence through strength:** The commentary argues that decisive U.S. action sends a clear message to hostile regimes that America will not allow nuclear threats or terror sponsors to operate unchecked, reinforcing the idea that peace is best preserved through strength and credibility.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|

**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[Same Colorado law, different outcomes: Probation in Denver, prison in Mesa County](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MARCH 4** _In Colorado, the same felony statute led to two very different courtroom outcomes. One walked away with probation. Peters is now serving a prison sentence that stretches close to a decade. The case against Peters unfolded under Colorado’s statute on attempting to influence a public servant—§ 18-8-306, the same law used in the prosecution of former Colorado state Sen. Sonya Jaquez Lewis._
**[Grassroots-backed election amendments fall short as House advances HB26-1113](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MARCH 3** _Colorado lawmakers approved a sweeping update to the state’s election laws Tuesday after rejecting several amendments that would have added voter roll verification requirements and expanded cybersecurity standards for election infrastructure._
**[Former Judicial Discipline Director Files Federal Lawsuit Challenging Colorado Supreme Court Oversight](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | MARCH 3** _A former top official inside Colorado’s judicial discipline system is accusing the state’s highest court of protecting itself — and says he was fired after trying to hold it accountable. Christopher S.P. Gregory’s federal lawsuit names an unusually broad group of defendants: the Colorado Judicial Discipline Rulemaking Committee, the Colorado Supreme Court, Governor Jared Polis, Attorney General Phil Weiser, current and former justices, senior judicial administrators, and other state officials._

This is an all-hands-on-deck moment: President Trump just said Republicans should “nationalize” elections and put Republicans in charge of state elections.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260305em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260305em]
Let’s be clear about what that means.
It means placing the administration of our elections under the personal control of a President who has already tried to overturn one election. And it means ripping up our Constitution because our wannabe dictator doesn’t like the results of an election he clearly lost. And it’s a clear signal he’s afraid of losing more elections and the accountability that will follow.
I won’t allow that to happen in Oregon.
States run elections. Not presidents. And as Oregon’s Secretary of State, I take that responsibility seriously — because democracy doesn’t defend itself.
We’ve beaten Trump-backed efforts in court before. We’ve already stopped him from forcing Oregon to give his Department of Justice access to your private voter data. And if he tries again, we’ll fight him again — and win again.
So here’s the bottom line: Trump can bluster on right-wing podcasts and cable news all he wants. He can threaten, lie, cheat, and moan about all the elections he’s lost.
But in Oregon, the rules still matter. The Constitution still matters. And intimidation will always fail.
I can’t do this alone, though. Taking on President Donald Trump and winning requires a strong grassroots network, so I’m asking you to stand with me and add your name to my petition today. Tell President Trump and anyone who enables him: Oregon’s elections are not yours to take. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/NrgrO3JQx0qx2yXRXfjF1A2]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/NrgrO3JQx0qx2yXRXfjF1A2]
This isn’t about party allegiance. This is about whether we let a would-be dictator decide who gets to vote and who wins elections.
I know where I stand. I’m counting on you to be there with me.
Thank you,
